These compounds represent a radically innovative approach by integrating direct antiviral activity—through selective inhibition of the NS2B‐NS3 protease and NS5 RNA polymerase—with the modulation of the inflammatory response, a key determinant in the progression of severe disease forms.The present study offers an in‐depth and innovative analysis of the therapeutic potential of these molecules, exploring in vitro and in silico assays and pharmacokinetic improvement strategies. The results reveal that TZDs and thiazoles have high affinity for strategic viral targets, effectively interrupting the DENV replication cycle and reducing the immunopathological effects of the infection. Unlike conventional antivirals, which fail to target a single mechanism of action, these molecules offer a multifunctional and disruptive approach, potentially redefining the treatment of dengue. By consolidating new therapeutic perspectives and providing a solid basis for future preclinical and clinical investigations, this study not only contributes to the advancement of biomedical science, but also represents a crucial milestone in the fight against one of the most neglected viruses in the world.
abstract_zh: 摘要 登革热是全球最大的健康危机之一,每年造成数百万例感染,且目前尚无有效的抗病毒药物疗法。高发病率和死亡率率,加上病毒的快速传播,凸显了在抗击该疾病过程中存在关键性的失败。在这种情况下,寻找新的抗病毒药物药物不仅必要,而且紧迫。最近,噻唑烷二酮(TZD)和噻唑衍生物被提出作为治疗的潜在候选药物,挑战了传统疗法的范式。这些化合物通过选择性抑制NS2B-NS3蛋白酶和NS5 RNA聚合酶,直接作用于抗病毒药物,同时调节免疫应答,这是严重疾病进展的关键决定因素。本研究提供了对这些分子治疗潜力的深入且创新的分析,探讨了体外和计算机模拟实验以及药代动力学改进策略。研究结果表明,TZDs和噻唑类化合物对关键病毒靶点具有高亲和力,能够有效中断DENV的复制周期,并减轻感染的免疫病理效应。与传统抗病毒药物药物不同,这些分子提供了一种多功能且具有破坏性的方法,可能重新定义登革热的治疗。通过整合新的治疗视角并为未来的临床前和临床研究提供坚实基础,本研究不仅推动了生物医学科学的发展,也标志着对抗全球最被忽视病毒之一的重要里程碑。

title: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever Case Prediction Using Climate and Social Media Data with Support Vector Regression
abstract: Dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) remains a recurring public health problem in Surabaya, with transmission influenced by climatic variability and potentially reflected in social media activity. This study aims to develop an informatics-based model for predicting annual DHF cases by integrating climate and Twitter/X data and comparing Support Vector Regression (SVR) with Ridge Regression. The dataset covers 2010–2024 and combines annual DHF case records, annual and seasonal climate indices from Juanda and Tanjung Perak stations, and 320 Indonesian-language tweets related to DHF in Surabaya. Social media data were transformed into annual tweet volume, negative-sentiment tweet volume, and mean sentiment score, while predictors were aligned using a one-year time lag. Model performance was evaluated using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation for 2011–2024 based on MAE, RMSE, and R2. SVR achieved the best performance with an MAE of 386.31 cases, RMSE of 556.86 cases, and R2 of 0.0121, outperforming Ridge Regression with an MAE of 601.31, RMSE of 727.19, and R2 of −0.6846. These findings indicate that SVR better captures nonlinear relationships in multisource dengue data, although explanatory power remains limited by few annual observations and high feature dimensionality. This study demonstrates the potential of multisource data integration for data-driven dengue early warning systems.

title_zh: 利用气候和社会媒体数据进行登革出血热病例预测的基于支持媒介回归的模型
source_body_en: Dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) remains a recurring public health problem in Surabaya, with transmission influenced by climatic variability and potentially reflected in social media activity. This study aims to develop an informatics-based model for predicting annual DHF cases by integrating climate and Twitter/X data and comparing Support Vector Regression (SVR) with Ridge Regression. The dataset covers 2010–2024 and combines annual DHF case records, annual and seasonal climate indices from Juanda and Tanjung Perak stations, and 320 Indonesian-language tweets related to DHF in Surabaya. Social media data were transformed into annual tweet volume, negative-sentiment tweet volume, and mean sentiment score, while predictors were aligned using a one-year time lag. Model performance was evaluated using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation for 2011–2024 based on MAE, RMSE, and R2. SVR achieved the best performance with an MAE of 386.31 cases, RMSE of 556.86 cases, and R2 of 0.0121, outperforming Ridge Regression with an MAE of 601.31, RMSE of 727.19, and R2 of −0.6846. These findings indicate that SVR better captures nonlinear relationships in multisource dengue data, although explanatory power remains limited by few annual observations and high feature dimensionality. This study demonstrates the potential of multisource data integration for data-driven dengue early warning systems.
abstract_zh: 登革出血热(DHF)仍然是苏腊巴亚地区反复出现的公共卫生问题,其传播受气候变异的影响,并可能在社交媒体活动中有体现。本研究旨在开发一个基于信息学的模型,通过整合气候数据和Twitter/X数据,预测年度DHF病例,并将支持媒介回归(SVR)与岭回归进行比较。数据集涵盖2010年至2024年,结合了年度DHF病例记录、Juanda和Tanjung Perak站点的年度和季节性气候指数,以及与苏腊巴亚地区DHF相关的320条印尼语推文。社交媒体数据被转换为年度推文数量、负面情绪推文数量和平均情绪得分,同时预测变量使用一年时间滞后进行对齐。模型性能通过2011年至2024年的留一法交叉验证(Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation)进行评估,依据MAE、RMSE和R2指标。SVR在MAE为386.31例、RMSE为556.86例、R2为0.0121的情况下表现最佳,优于岭回归的MAE为601.31、RMSE为727.19和R2为−0.6846。这些发现表明,SVR在多源登革热数据中更好地捕捉了非线性关系,尽管其解释力仍受到年度观察数据较少和高特征维度的限制。本研究展示了多源数据整合在数据驱动的登革热早期预警系统中的潜力。

title: Association of dengue severity with the serotype of infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Dengue is a mosquito-borne infection caused by one of four dengue virus serotypes (DENV1-4) that circulates endemically across the tropics and subtropics. To date, there is contrasting evidence on the relationship between the serotype of infection and disease severity. Methods We conducted a systematic review (PROSPERO, CRD42023443101) and meta-analysis to examine the association between the serotype of symptomatic infections with severe disease while accounting for both prior exposure status and geographic region, with 18 severity defined by (i) the 1997 World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines, (ii) the 2009 WHO guidelines or (iii) hospitalisation. We searched the Global Health, Embase Classic + Embase, and Medline databases using Ovid for studies published up to 20 January 2025 and extracted case counts with matched serotype and severity information. We fitted generalised linear mixed models to estimate the proportions of severe cases, running independent analyses per severity definition, and stratifying by prior exposure-serotype combinations (e.g. primary DENV2) and geographic region (Asia versus Americas). Heterogeneity was assessed using the τ 26 and I metrics and risk of bias was assessed by adapting an established tool for risk of bias in prevalence studies. 28 Findings Our search yielded 4621 unique records, with 71 studies included for the meta-analysis. We found that, on average, DENV3 in Asia resulted in the highest proportion of DHF/DSS (21·00% [95% CrI: 13·02 to 30·44%]) and hospitalised (22·00% [95% CrI: 0·88 to 75·31%]) cases among symptomatic primary infections, while also causing the highest proportion

analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines the association between the serotype of dengue virus infection and disease severity, focusing on symptomatic primary infections and their outcomes, including severe dengue, dengue hemorrhagic fever, dengue shock syndrome, and hospitalisation. The central question is whether specific dengue virus serotypes are linked to higher severity of disease.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a systematic search of the Global Health, Embase Classic + Embase, and Medline databases using Ovid, including studies published up to 20 January 2025. The eligibility criteria included studies with matched serotype and severity information. A meta-analysis was performed using generalised linear mixed models, stratifying by prior exposure-serotype combinations and geographic region (Asia versus Americas). Heterogeneity was assessed using τ2 and I2 metrics, and risk of bias was evaluated using an adapted tool for prevalence studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The meta-analysis found that DENV3 in Asia resulted in the highest proportion of dengue hemorrhagic fever/dengue shock syndrome (DHF/DSS) cases among symptomatic primary infections, with an average of 21·00% [95% CrI: 13·02 to 30·44%]. It also showed that DENV3 caused the highest proportion of hospitalised cases (22·00% [95% CrI: 0·88 to 75·31%]) among primary infections.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is contrasting evidence on the relationship between serotype and disease severity. The review highlights heterogeneity in findings and the need for further research to clarify the role of serotype in disease severity across different geographic regions and exposure statuses.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to understand the mechanisms by which specific serotypes contribute to disease severity and to explore the impact of geographic region and prior exposure on outcomes. Surveillance and diagnostic efforts should consider serotype-specific patterns in disease severity to improve public health responses.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigate the association between dengue virus serotype and disease severity, focusing on symptomatic primary infections. The study included 71 studies from a search of Global Health, Embase Classic + Embase, and Medline databases up to 20 January 2025. The analysis used generalised linear mixed models to estimate severe case proportions, stratifying by serotype and geographic region. The findings suggest that DENV3 in Asia is associated with the highest proportion of severe dengue cases, including dengue hemorrhagic fever/dengue shock syndrome and hospitalisation. However, the review notes contrasting evidence and heterogeneity in results, highlighting the need for further research to clarify serotype-specific impacts on disease severity.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述探讨了感染血清型与疾病严重程度之间的关联,重点关注有症状的初次感染及其结果,包括登革热、登革出血热、登革休克综合征和住院情况。核心问题是特定血清型是否与更高的疾病严重程度相关。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 综述通过Ovid检索了Global Health、Embase Classic + Embase和Medline数据库,包括截至2025年1月20日发表的研究。纳入标准包括具有匹配血清型和严重程度信息的研究。采用广义线性混合模型进行了荟萃分析,并按先前暴露-血清型组合和地理区域(亚洲与美洲)进行分层。异质性通过τ2和I2指标进行评估,偏倚风险则通过修改后的适用于患病率研究的偏倚风险评估工具进行评估。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 荟萃分析发现,在亚洲地区,DENV3在有症状的初次感染中导致的登革出血热/登革休克综合征(DHF/DSS)病例比例最高,平均为21·00% [95% CrI: 13·02至30·44%]。它还表明,DENV3在初次感染中导致的住院病例比例最高,为22·00% [95% CrI: 0·88至75·31%]。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 关于血清型与疾病严重程度之间的关系存在相互矛盾的证据。综述强调了研究结果的异质性,并指出需要进一步研究以明确不同地理区域和暴露状态中血清型在疾病严重程度中的作用。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要进一步研究以了解特定血清型如何导致疾病严重程度,并探讨地理区域和先前暴露对结果的影响。监测和诊断工作应考虑疾病严重程度的血清型特异性模式,以提高公共卫生应对措施。

title: Shared evidence, different recommendations: a comparative analysis of Qdenga (TAK-003) dengue vaccine guidance for travellers across countries.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Dengue is an increasingly important cause of illness in travellers, and Qdenga (TAK-003) is the first dengue vaccine incorporated into guidance for travellers in multiple countries. However, clinicians and travellers may encounter differing recommendations across jurisdictions. This study compared guidance on the use of Qdenga in travellers across countries. METHODS: We conducted a comparative analysis of national guidance on Qdenga use for travellers across countries, using survey data and structured review of publicly available recommendations. Guidance was synthesized according to dengue immune status and mapped across recurring decision domains. RESULTS: Survey responses were obtained from 18 advisory bodies across 17 countries between March and April 2026, including 12 non-endemic countries where Qdenga was licensed and guidance published. Guidance was generally more restrictive than regulatory authorization. While there was broad agreement in recommending vaccination for travellers with laboratory-confirmed prior dengue infection, recommendations for those without documented infection varied widely. All advisory bodies considered destination-specific dengue risk but differed in whether and how they used travel duration, repeated or cumulative exposure, traveller characteristics and host susceptibility factors to determine vaccine eligibility. Some recommendations restricted vaccination to travellers with prior dengue infection, whereas others extended eligibility to selected travellers without documented prior infection or recommended vaccination based on exposure risk, irrespective of serostatus. Approaches also differed in assessment of prior dengue infection and whether completion of the two-dose series before travel was required. CONCLUSIONS: Variation in Qdenga guidance reflects differences in how advisory bodies interpret shared evidence and manage uncertainty arising from data gaps and differences between trial populations and travellers. Additional data on vaccine effectiveness and clinical outcomes among seronegative travellers and older adults may help reduce uncertainty and support greater alignment of future recommendations. Regardless, transparency and shared clinical decision-making remain essential when discussing dengue vaccination with travellers.

abstract_zh: 引言:登革热正成为旅行者疾病的一个日益重要的原因,而Qdenga(TAK-003)是首个被纳入多个国家旅行者指南的登革热疫苗。然而,临床医生和旅行者可能在不同司法管辖区遇到不同的建议。本研究比较了各国对Qdenga在旅行者中使用指南的差异。方法:我们对多个国家关于Qdenga用于旅行者指南进行了比较分析,利用调查数据和公开可用指南的结构化审查。根据登革热免疫状态对指南进行了综合,并映射到反复出现的决策领域。结果:2026年3月至4月期间,从17个国家的18个咨询机构获得了调查回复,包括12个非疫区国家,这些国家已批准Qdenga并发布了指南。指南通常比监管授权更为严格。尽管在推荐疫苗接种给有实验室确认既往登革热感染的旅行者方面存在广泛共识,但对无既往感染记录的旅行者推荐则差异较大。所有咨询机构都考虑了目的地特定的登革热风险,但在是否以及如何使用旅行时长、重复或累积暴露、旅行者特征和宿主易感因素来决定疫苗资格方面存在差异。一些指南仅将疫苗接种推荐给有既往登革热感染的旅行者,而另一些则扩展资格至部分无既往感染记录的旅行者,或根据暴露风险推荐疫苗接种,而不论血清状态。在评估既往登革热感染以及是否需要在旅行前完成两剂系列接种方面也存在不同方法。结论:Qdenga指南的差异反映了咨询机构在解释共享证据和处理因数据缺口及试验人群与旅行者之间的差异而产生的不确定性时的不同方式。关于疫苗在血清阴性旅行者和老年人中的有效性及临床结果的额外数据可能有助于减少不确定性,并支持未来建议的更大一致性。无论如何,透明度和共享的临床决策仍然是与旅行者讨论登革热疫苗接种时的关键要素。

title: Dengue virus 2 lacking N153 glycosylation displayed enhanced recognition by neutralizing antibodies
abstract: Abstract Deglycosylated (N153Q) dengue virus (DENV) mutant shows attenuated infection in a mouse model, mainly due to its increased antibody susceptibility. This is consistent with the neutralization assay showing human monoclonal antibodies 2D22 and C10 are more potent towards the mutant than the wild-type (WT) virus. Here, we compared the cryoEM structures of WT and mutant viruses complexed with these Fabs at 37 °C (2.7–3.2 Å resolution). We observed increased occupancies for both Fabs on the mutant virus, suggesting higher accessibility of epitopes that were previously blocked by glycosylation. Using biolayer interferometry, we showed that at 30 °C, the antibodies exhibited a slower binding rate with the mutant than with WT virus, along with a slower dissociation rate. However, at 37 °C, the affinities of both antibodies for DENV2 WT and N153Q increased significantly. N153Q mutant might be a good vaccine candidate, as important epitopes are made more accessible for stimulating highly potent antibodies.

title: Temporal trends in dengue incidence and mortality across surveillance case classifications: a 13-year analysis from Davao City, Philippines
abstract: Introduction Dengue remains a major public health concern in the Philippines, where routine surveillance systems classify reported cases as suspected, probable or confirmed. Although these classifications are widely used to monitor disease burden, their influence on the interpretation of long-term epidemiological trends and mortality patterns remains unclear. This study examined the temporal trends in dengue incidence and mortality across surveillance case classifications in Davao City, Philippines, over a 13-year period. Methods A retrospective observational study was conducted using dengue surveillance data collected from the Philippine Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (PIDSR) system from January 2012 to December 2024. Reported dengue cases were classified as suspected, probable, or confirmed, according to the national surveillance definitions. Annual dengue incidence and mortality were calculated per 100,000 population, and temporal trends were assessed using the Mann–Kendall trend test. Results A total of 81,075 dengue cases were reported during the study period, including 59,021 suspected, 20,559 probable, and 1,495 confirmed cases. Confirmed dengue incidence exhibited a significant increasing trend over time ( p = 0.003), whereas probable ( p = 0.855) and suspected dengue incidences ( p = 0.059) showed no statistically significant temporal trends. Increasing trends in confirmed dengue incidence were consistently observed across congressional districts, age groups, and sexes. Dengue mortality incidence showed no significant temporal trends in suspected ( p = 0.089), probable ( p = 0.242), or confirmed cases ( p = 0.282). Most deaths recorded among reported dengue notifications occurred among probable and suspected cases, and the highest cumulative case fatality rate was observed among probable cases (0.89%). Conclusion Surveillance classifications captured distinct epidemiological patterns of dengue incidence and mortality. In low- and middle-income country (LMIC) settings, where surveillance systems operate under varying levels of diagnostic certainty, considering probable and suspected case classifications may provide additional insights into surveillance trends and mortality patterns beyond those obtained from laboratory-confirmed cases.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the temporal trends in dengue incidence and mortality across different surveillance classifications in Davao City, Philippines, over a 13-year period. It found that confirmed dengue cases showed a significant increasing trend, while probable and suspected cases did not. Dengue mortality also showed no significant trends across classifications. Most deaths occurred among probable and suspected cases, with the highest case fatality rate observed in probable cases. The study highlights the importance of considering different case classifications in understanding dengue epidemiology, especially in low- and middle-income countries where diagnostic certainty may vary. The findings suggest that surveillance data may provide additional insights into disease trends and mortality patterns beyond those obtained from laboratory-confirmed cases. The study is based on retrospective observational data and uses the Mann–Kendall trend test to assess trends.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热仍然是菲律宾的主要公共卫生问题,其中常规的监测系统将报告的病例分为疑似、可能和确认三类。尽管这些分类被广泛用于监测疾病负担,但它们对长期流行病学趋势和死亡率模式的解释影响尚不明确。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了菲律宾达瓦奥市在13年期间,登革热发病率和死亡率在监测病例分类中的时间趋势。采用回顾性观察设计,使用菲律宾集成疾病监测和响应(PIDSR)系统从2012年1月至2024年12月收集的登革热监测数据。研究期间共报告了81,075例登革热病例,包括59,021例疑似病例、20,559例可能病例和1,495例确认病例。
elements_zh.methods: Annual dengue incidence and mortality were calculated per 100,000 population, and temporal trends were assessed using the Mann–Kendall trend test. Reported dengue cases were classified as suspected, probable, or confirmed, according to the national surveillance definitions.
elements_zh.main_results: 确认的登革热发病率显示出随时间显著上升的趋势(p = 0.003),而可能(p = 0.855)和疑似登革热发病率(p = 0.059)则未显示出统计学上显著的时间趋势。登革热死亡率在疑似(p = 0.089)、可能(p = 0.242)和确认病例(p = 0.282)中均未显示出显著的时间趋势。在报告的登革热病例中,大多数死亡病例发生在可能和疑似病例中,而可能病例的最高累积病例死亡率(0.89%)被观察到。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 监测分类捕捉了登革热发病率和死亡率不同的流行病学模式。确认的登革热发病率上升趋势在国会选区、年龄组和性别中均一致观察到。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 在低收入和中等收入国家(LMIC)中,由于监测系统在诊断确定性方面存在不同水平,考虑可能和疑似病例分类可能提供超出实验室确认病例所获得的额外见解,以理解监测趋势和死亡率模式。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告研究设计的局限性或证据强度评估。

title_zh: 菲律宾达瓦奥市登革热发病率和死亡率在监测病例分类中的时间趋势:一项为期13年的分析
source_body_en: Introduction Dengue remains a major public health concern in the Philippines, where routine surveillance systems classify reported cases as suspected, probable or confirmed. Although these classifications are widely used to monitor disease burden, their influence on the interpretation of long-term epidemiological trends and mortality patterns remains unclear. This study examined the temporal trends in dengue incidence and mortality across surveillance case classifications in Davao City, Philippines, over a 13-year period. Methods A retrospective observational study was conducted using dengue surveillance data collected from the Philippine Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (PIDSR) system from January 2012 to December 2024. Reported dengue cases were classified as suspected, probable, or confirmed, according to the national surveillance definitions. Annual dengue incidence and mortality were calculated per 100,000 population, and temporal trends were assessed using the Mann–Kendall trend test. Results A total of 81,075 dengue cases were reported during the study period, including 59,021 suspected, 20,559 probable, and 1,495 confirmed cases. Confirmed dengue incidence exhibited a significant increasing trend over time ( p = 0.003), whereas probable ( p = 0.855) and suspected dengue incidences ( p = 0.059) showed no statistically significant temporal trends. Increasing trends in confirmed dengue incidence were consistently observed across congressional districts, age groups, and sexes. Dengue mortality incidence showed no significant temporal trends in suspected ( p = 0.089), probable ( p = 0.242), or confirmed cases ( p = 0.282). Most deaths recorded among reported dengue notifications occurred among probable and suspected cases, and the highest cumulative case fatality rate was observed among probable cases (0.89%). Conclusion Surveillance classifications captured distinct epidemiological patterns of dengue incidence and mortality. In low- and middle-income country (LMIC) settings, where surveillance systems operate under varying levels of diagnostic certainty, considering probable and suspected case classifications may provide additional insights into surveillance trends and mortality patterns beyond those obtained from laboratory-confirmed cases.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热仍然是菲律宾的主要公共卫生问题,其中常规的监测系统将报告的病例分为疑似、可能和确认三类。尽管这些分类被广泛用于监测疾病负担,但它们对长期流行病学趋势和死亡率模式的解释影响尚不明确。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了菲律宾达瓦奥市在13年期间,登革热发病率和死亡率在监测病例分类中的时间趋势。采用回顾性观察设计,使用菲律宾集成疾病监测和响应(PIDSR)系统从2012年1月至2024年12月收集的登革热监测数据。研究期间共报告了81,075例登革热病例,包括59,021例疑似病例、20,559例可能病例和1,495例确认病例。
analysis_zh.main_results: 确认的登革热发病率显示出随时间显著上升的趋势(p = 0.003),而可能(p = 0.855)和疑似登革热发病率(p = 0.059)则未显示出统计学上显著的时间趋势。登革热死亡率在疑似(p = 0.089)、可能(p = 0.242)和确认病例(p = 0.282)中均未显示出显著的时间趋势。在报告的登革热病例中,大多数死亡病例发生在可能和疑似病例中,而可能病例的最高累积病例死亡率(0.89%)被观察到。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 监测分类捕捉了登革热发病率和死亡率不同的流行病学模式。确认的登革热发病率上升趋势在国会选区、年龄组和性别中均一致观察到。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 在低收入和中等收入国家(LMIC)中,由于监测系统在诊断确定性方面存在不同水平,考虑可能和疑似病例分类可能提供超出实验室确认病例所获得的额外见解,以理解监测趋势和死亡率模式。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告研究设计的局限性或证据强度评估。

title: Relationship between Knowledge and Attitudes in the Community with Dengue Fever Preventive Behavior in Landasan Ulin Utara Village
abstract: Background: The incidence of dengue fever in Landasan Ulin Utara Village remains high, with an outbreak status. The elevated case incidence may be attributed to insufficient community knowledge and awareness, ultimately contributing to inadequate dengue prevention behaviors. Objectives: Analyze the relationship between community knowledge and attitudes and dengue fever prevention behaviors in Landasan Ulin Utara Village. Methods: This cross-sectional study involved 164 heads of households or family members aged 15–64 years in Landasan Ulin Utara Village. Individual respondents were the unit of analysis. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed using Spearman’s rho test. Results: Based on the statistical test results, it was found that there was no correlation between community knowledge and attitudes and dengue fever prevention practices in Landasan Ulin Utara Village (p = 0.193; p = 0.150). Conclusion: There are several factors that can influence dengue prevention behavior among the community in Landasan Ulin Utara Village, including education level, experience, type of work, social environment, culture, media exposure, and emotional factors.

title_zh: 兰达森乌林北村社区知识与态度与登革热预防行为的关系
source_body_en: Background: The incidence of dengue fever in Landasan Ulin Utara Village remains high, with an outbreak status. The elevated case incidence may be attributed to insufficient community knowledge and awareness, ultimately contributing to inadequate dengue prevention behaviors. Objectives: Analyze the relationship between community knowledge and attitudes and dengue fever prevention behaviors in Landasan Ulin Utara Village. Methods: This cross-sectional study involved 164 heads of households or family members aged 15–64 years in Landasan Ulin Utara Village. Individual respondents were the unit of analysis. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed using Spearman’s rho test. Results: Based on the statistical test results, it was found that there was no correlation between community knowledge and attitudes and dengue fever prevention practices in Landasan Ulin Utara Village (p = 0.193; p = 0.150). Conclusion: There are several factors that can influence dengue prevention behavior among the community in Landasan Ulin Utara Village, including education level, experience, type of work, social environment, culture, media exposure, and emotional factors.

title: Retrospective and Contemporary Genomic Surveillance Reveals Genotype-Specific Dengue Lineage Dynamics in Rio de Janeiro
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) transmission in Brazil is characterized by recurrent epidemics involving the introduction, persistence, and replacement of viral lineages. However, temporal gaps in genomic surveillance limit our understanding of how these processes shape successive epidemics in Rio de Janeiro. Here, in a retrospective observational molecular epidemiology study, we combined archived genomic data with publicly available sequences and epidemiological surveillance data to investigate the temporal dynamics of DENV serotypes and lineages in Rio de Janeiro. Archived DENV-positive samples were curated and subjected to whole-genome amplicon sequencing, and the resulting consensus sequences were analyzed together with publicly available sequences using time-scaled phylogenetic reconstruction and epidemiological data. We recovered 35 DENV genomes from samples collected in 2013, 2018, 2020, and 2021, including DENV-1 genotype V, DENV-2 genotypes II and III, and DENV-4 genotype II. Analysis of the combined datasets identified multiple Rio de Janeiro-associated clades with distinct temporal patterns. Publicly available sequences supported the broader clade structure and long-term temporal patterns independently of most genomes generated here. The newly generated genomes made genotype-specific contributions: the five DENV-1 genotype V genomes placed archived 2020–2021 samples within previously represented Rio de Janeiro-associated groups, while the single DENV-2 genotype II genome provided phylogenetic placement of a travel-associated 2018 case. In contrast, the 20 DENV-2 genotype III genomes identified a Rio de Janeiro-associated cluster not represented among the public sequences, and the nine DENV-4 genotype II genomes increased representation of the 2013 epidemic. Thus, the principal contribution of retrospective sequencing was to fill specific temporal and geographic gaps rather than to redefine the broader historical phylogenetic structure of all genotypes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the temporal dynamics of dengue virus (DENV) serotypes and lineages in Rio de Janeiro by combining archived genomic data with publicly available sequences and epidemiological surveillance. The research highlights the importance of genomic surveillance in understanding the introduction, persistence, and replacement of viral lineages during recurrent epidemics. The study recovered 35 DENV genomes, including DENV-1 genotype V, DENV-2 genotypes II and III, and DENV-4 genotype II, from samples collected between 2013 and 2021. The findings reveal distinct temporal patterns and identify a DENV-2 genotype III cluster not previously represented in public sequences. The study emphasizes the role of retrospective sequencing in filling specific gaps rather than redefining broader historical phylogenetic structures. The results contribute to the understanding of DENV lineage dynamics and have implications for surveillance and public health strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 巴西的登革病毒(DENV)传播以反复暴发为特征,涉及病毒谱系的引入、持续存在和替代。然而,基因组监测的时间间隔限制了我们对这些过程如何塑造里约热内卢连续暴发的理解。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这里,我们进行了一项回顾性观察性分子流行病学研究,结合了存档的基因组数据、公开可用的序列和流行病学监测数据,以研究里约热内卢DENV血清型和谱系的时间动态。
elements_zh.methods: 存档的DENV阳性样本经过整理,并进行全基因组扩增子测序,所得的共识序列与公开可用的序列一起,通过时间尺度系统发育重建和流行病学数据进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 我们从2013年、2018年、2020年和2021年采集的样本中恢复了35个DENV 基因组,包括DENV-1基因型V、DENV-2基因型II和III以及DENV-4基因型II。对综合数据集的分析识别出多个与里约热内卢相关的谱系,具有不同的时间模式。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 公开可用的序列独立于此处生成的大多数基因组,支持了更广泛的谱系结构和长期时间模式。新生成的基因组在基因型层面做出了贡献:五个DENV-1基因型V 基因组将存档的2020–2021年样本置于之前已代表的里约热内卢相关群体中,而单个DENV-2基因型II 基因组则提供了与旅行相关的2018年病例的系统发育定位。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 相比之下,20个DENV-2基因型III 基因组识别出一个未在公开序列中出现的里约热内卢相关簇,而九个DENV-4基因型II 基因组则增加了2013年暴发的代表性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 因此,回顾性测序的主要贡献在于填补特定的时间和地理空白,而不是重新定义所有基因型的更广泛历史系统发育结构。

abstract_zh: 巴西的登革病毒(DENV)传播以反复暴发为特征,涉及病毒谱系的引入、持续存在和替代。然而,基因组监测的时间间隔限制了我们对这些过程如何塑造里约热内卢连续暴发的理解。在这里,我们进行了一项回顾性观察性分子流行病学研究,结合了存档的基因组数据、公开可用的序列和流行病学监测数据,以研究里约热内卢DENV血清型和谱系的时间动态。存档的DENV阳性样本经过整理,并进行全基因组扩增子测序,所得的共识序列与公开可用的序列一起,通过时间尺度系统发育重建和流行病学数据进行分析。我们从2013年、2018年、2020年和2021年采集的样本中恢复了35个DENV 基因组,包括DENV-1基因型V、DENV-2基因型II和III以及DENV-4基因型II。对综合数据集的分析识别出多个与里约热内卢相关的谱系,具有不同的时间模式。公开可用的序列独立于此处生成的大多数基因组,支持了更广泛的谱系结构和长期时间模式。新生成的基因组在基因型层面做出了贡献:五个DENV-1基因型V 基因组将存档的2020–2021年样本置于之前已代表的里约热内卢相关群体中,而单个DENV-2基因型II 基因组则提供了与旅行相关的2018年病例的系统发育定位。相比之下,20个DENV-2基因型III 基因组识别出一个未在公开序列中出现的里约热内卢相关簇,而九个DENV-4基因型II 基因组则增加了2013年暴发的代表性。因此,回顾性测序的主要贡献在于填补特定的时间和地理空白,而不是重新定义所有基因型的更广泛历史系统发育结构。

title: Dengue Virus Evasion of Host Innate Immunity
abstract: Infection with dengue virus (DENV) is a major global public health threat, driven by mosquito transmission of four closely related virus serotypes. For effective transmission between hosts, DENV rapidly remodels the host cell to overcome multiple innate immune barriers and produce progeny virions. Here we review how DENV evades cell-intrinsic sensing and interferon (IFN) responses in both human and mosquito hosts. We highlight the roles of replication organelles, nonstructural proteins NS2B/3 and NS5, and subgenomic flaviviral RNAs in escaping RIG-I-like receptor and cGAS-STING signaling, disrupting JAK-STAT pathways, and subverting autophagy and ER-phagy. We further discuss NS1-mediated vascular leak, exploitation of TAM receptors, serotype-specific differences in IFN antagonism, and how these mechanisms might shape pathogenesis, host range, and epidemiological fitness. Finally, we consider how defined immune evasion strategies inform rational design of antivirals and next-generation live-attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccines to mitigate the escalating global dengue burden.

Here we review how DENV evades cell-intrinsic sensing and interferon (IFN) responses in both human and mosquito hosts. We highlight the roles of replication organelles, nonstructural proteins NS2B/3 and NS5, and subgenomic flaviviral RNAs in escaping RIG-I-like receptor and cGAS-STING signaling, disrupting JAK-STAT pathways, and subverting autophagy and ER-phagy. We further discuss NS1-mediated vascular leak, exploitation of TAM receptors, serotype-specific differences in IFN antagonism, and how these mechanisms might shape pathogenesis, host range, and epidemiological fitness. Finally, we consider how defined immune evasion strategies inform rational design of antivirals and next-generation live-attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccines to mitigate the escalating global dengue burden.

title: Post-Dengue Syndrome: From Immunopathogenesis to Multisystemic Clinical Sequelae
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) causes the most prevalent arboviral infection worldwide. Although classically regarded as an acute illness, growing evidence describes Post-Dengue Syndrome (PDS) as a chronic entity affecting a subset of patients, with pooled estimates placing post-infectious fatigue at 20.0% (95% CI 10–36) and no standardized case definition yet available. This narrative review analyzes its pathophysiology: the cytokine storm, antibody-dependent enhancement, and NS1-triggered molecular mimicry, together with the cells that execute them—dendritic cells, mononuclear phagocytes, NK cells, platelets, and complement on the innate side, and plasmablast expansion, follicular helper T cell activation, defective regulatory control, and PD-L1/PD-1-mediated exhaustion on the adaptive side. Almost all of these immunological mechanisms have been characterized during acute infection; few studies have sampled the same patients during convalescence, and even fewer have compared those who developed persistent symptoms with those who recovered. They are therefore established features of acute dengue and, at present, hypotheses about PDS rather than demonstrated features. Genetic susceptibility is examined through polymorphisms of HLA, FcγRIIa, Toll-like receptor, and cytokine genes. Multisystemic manifestations are described—persistent fatigue, fibromyalgia-like myalgia and arthralgia, alopecia, brain fog, and mood disturbance—alongside neurological complications, categorized into direct neuroinvasion and post-infectious immune-mediated damage such as Guillain–Barré syndrome and encephalomyelitis. Recent population-based data linking dengue to acute neurological events and to later cognitive decline are examined critically, as is the unsettled question of whether post-dengue neuroinflammation amounts to neurodegeneration. Finally, the authors address the influence of age and sex and outline therapeutic and research priorities, offering an immunoclinical perspective for the multidisciplinary management of these patients.

title: Barriers in operating proactive source reduction informed by an early warning system for dengue prevention: A qualitative study from end-user perspectives in Vietnam.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue is a major vector-borne disease, with rising incidence driven by climate change, rapid urbanization, and increased international travel. Although early warning systems (EWSs) have shown promising predictive performance in endemic settings, limited evidence on implementation barriers from local end users hinders their integration into routine proactive vector control. METHODS: A qualitative study with in-depth interviews was conducted with local end users, including local authorities, health practitioners, and health volunteers. A deductive approach utilizing a predefined conceptual framework was employed to code the verbatim transcripts. Inductive coding was subsequently incorporated to capture emerging concepts that were not represented in the initial framework. Thematic analysis was performed to analyse the collected data. To enhance the methodological rigor, interviews and coding were performed by multiple and diverse researchers from various academic and practice institutions, and the transcripts were validated through member checking with selected participants. RESULTS: The lack of supportive policies, limited engagement from relevant stakeholders due to low familiarity with EWS concepts, and operational challenges were identified as critical barriers to implementing EWS-informed proactive source reduction. The perception that dengue risks were only during the rainy season, together with socio-economic constraints, water scarcity exacerbated by extreme weather events, and the application of inappropriate source reduction measures, further constrained household participation. The multi-level barriers collectively disrupted the translation of EWS alerts into proactive dengue prevention. CONCLUSIONS: Early warning information alone is insufficient to translate into effective and sustained proactive vector control for dengue prevention. Strengthening enabling policies, local stakeholder and community engagement, and awareness of EWS-informed risk management across multiple levels are essential to translate EWS alerts into timely and sustained vector control actions in dengue-endemic settings similar to Vietnam. Further studies across diverse settings are needed to assess the broader applicability of EWS-informed approaches.

title: Seroprevalence of Dengue Infection in Lahore During Rainfall Season of 2024
abstract: Objective: To determine the seroprevalence of dengue virus (DENV) IgM and IgG antibodies among clinically suspected dengue cases from different population groups in Lahore during the 2024 rainfall season. Study Design: Cross-sectional study. Place and Duration of Study: Department of Virology, Chughtai Institute of Pathology Lahore, Pakistan from Jul to Dec 2024. Methodology: A total of 681 clinically suspected dengue cases from various age groups were included. Serum samples were tested for anti-dengue IgM and IgG antibodies using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). IgM and IgG results were analyzed independently. Results: Of the 681 cases, 70.3% (n=479) were seropositive for dengue IgM antibodies, while 17.9% (n=122) were seropositive for dengue IgG antibodies. The highest proportion of IgG seropositivity was observed in the (25–44) year age group. September recorded the highest number of IgM-positive cases, accounting for 51.9% (n=249) of all IgM seropositive cases. Conclusion: A substantial proportion of suspected dengue cases in Lahore showed evidence of recent and past dengue infection during the monsoon season. These findings highlight seasonal dengue transmission and support the need for continued surveillance during peak periods.

title: Dengue Awareness Among Medical Students Of Public Sector Colleges, Lahore; A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: BACKGROUND & OBJECTIVE: Dengue is one of the most rapidly spreading viral disease transmitted by mosquito bite to human. In Pakistan, where dengue outbreaks have been a concern, increasing dengue awareness among medical students is vital. The objective of this study was to assess the current level of awareness about dengue, focusing related knowledge and practices.METHODOLOGY: This cross-sectional comparative study was conducted among 222 fourth year medical students selected through convenient sampling from six public sector medical colleges of Lahore. All those who were present at the time of data collection and were willing to participate were included but participants with incomplete responses were excluded from study. Data entry and analysis was done using SPSS version 27. A Pearson chi-square test of independence was conducted to evaluate the relationship between gender and dengue awareness scores. An independent-samples t-test was conducted to determine whether overall dengue knowledge scores differed significantly between day scholars and hostelite. A one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was conducted to evaluate differences in dengue awareness scores across six medical institutions in Lahore. A p-value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant scoring system was developed using all of the 27 questions of our online questionnaire, giving each correct question 1 score and incorrect as 0 score. ≥75% score considered as High level of awareness.RESULTS: Descriptive analysis of the 27-point dengue awareness scale showed almost identical awareness scores among male and female students. The scores in both groups ranged from 13.50 to 27.00, with an interquartile range of 4.50. For residential status, day scholars had a mean awareness score of 21.98 ± 2.81 and Hostelite had a mean score of 21.96 ± 3.26. No statistically significant association was found between gender and dengue awareness; similarly residential status was not significantly associated with dengue awareness. Although the mean awareness scores varied between institutions, ranging from 20.39 ± 4.01 at Fatima Jinnah Medical University to 23.18 ± 2.41 at Shaikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Medical and Dental College, this difference did not reach statistical significance.CONCLUSION: This multi-center study demonstrated high baseline dengue awareness among undergraduate medical students across public medical colleges in Lahore. Knowledge levels were uniform across demographic subgroups, showing no statistically significant differences by gender, or residential status. Although the mean awareness scores varied between institutions, this difference did not reach statistical significance. The difference of highest percentageof high level of awareness amongst different institute's emphasis need for more comprehensive sharing of information

title: Epidemiology of Dengue and its Association with Community Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices in Jazan, Saudi Arabia, (2020–2025)
abstract: Dengue remains a major public-health concern in southwestern Saudi Arabia, where local surveillance and community prevention are both essential. This study used the combination of retrospective surveillance and cross-sectional Knowledge, Attitude and Practices (KAP) assessment in Jazan Region. The number of laboratory confirmed dengue cases reported via the Saudi Ministry of Health HESN Plus (Health Electronic Surveillance Network) system from 2020 until 2025 was included in Component A. There were 430 adult primary healthcare (PHC) visitors who answered the structured KAP questionnaire in component B. Case counts were totaled and inter-year comparisons were made; KAP data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, nonparametric tests, Spearman correlations, reliability analysis, and multiple linear regression. Confirmed cases varied markedly across the study period: 33 in 2020, 24 in 2021, 177 in 2022, 270 in 2023, 452 in 2024, and 32 in 2025. The distribution of the number of counts across the year was not equal (χ2(5, N=988) = 902.01, p

title: Dengue Shock Syndrome With Pleural Effusion in Pediatrics : A Case-Based Review
abstract: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) remains a significant public health concern in Indonesia. This article reports describes the case of an 8-year-10-month-old girl presenting with a five-day history of persistent fever accompanied by generalized weakness, headache, epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. Upon admission, physical examination revealed a criticallly ill patient weighing 28 kilograms, with clinical signs of shock, including tachycardia, tachypnea, cold extremities, delayed capillary refill, and minimal pleural effusion on chest radiography. Laboratory findings revealed thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, hypokalemia, hyponatremia and hemoconcentration. A working diagnosis of Dengue Shock Syndrome (DSS) with electrolyte imbalance was established. The patient received fluid resuscitation, inotropic, supportive therapy and family education regarding disease course and prognosis. This case highlights the importance of early recognition, prompt management, and close monitoring of pediatric patients with severe dengue manifestations to prevent potentially fatal complications.

title: Biogenic flavonoid capping converts a cytotoxic Carica papaya fraction into a selective, cross-serotype Dengue entry inhibitor
abstract: Plant-derived flavonoids show measurable anti-dengue activity in cell culture, but their translational value is limited by a narrow therapeutic window: the concentrations that inhibit the virus approach or exceed those that are cytotoxic. Whether nanoparticle formulation can resolve this constraint, rather than simply add potency, remains untested for a chemically defined fraction. Here we show that biogenic silver nanoparticle (AgNP) formation using a flavonoid-enriched fraction of Carica papaya inverts an unusable selectivity profile into a viable one. The unformulated fraction was cytotoxic below the concentrations required for antiviral activity: its 50% cytotoxic concentration (CC50 = 134.9 ug/mL) lay below its 50% effective concentration against dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2; EC50 = 254.4 ug/mL), giving a Selectivity Index (SI) of 0.53. Using the same flavonoids as sole reducing and capping agents produced AgNPs (Z-average 128.4 nm; PDI 0.232; zeta potential -28.4 mV) that moved both parameters simultaneously. CC50 rose approximately 8.6-fold to 1,165.74 ug/mL while EC50 fell approximately 8.8-fold to 29.05 ug/mL, raising the SI to 40.12, an approximately 75-fold shift. Time-of-addition analysis localised the effect to the extracellular phase: inhibition was significant under pre-treatment and co-treatment but not after viral adsorption, identifying the AgNPs as entry inhibitors rather than replication inhibitors. Consistent with a serotype-independent physical mechanism, AgNP treatment at 30 ug/mL reduced viral RNA across all four serotypes, using inocula standardised against WHO-traceable NAAT reference reagents. These findings identify capping chemistry, rather than silver content alone, as a determinant of the therapeutic window in phytosynthesised nanoantivirals.

title: Saúde Única e adequação climática: transposição fronteiriça de dengue e leishmaniose nas áreas temperadas e subtropicais do Cone Sul One Health and climate suitability: shifting frontiers of dengue and leishmaniasis in the subtropical and temperate areas of the Southern Cone
abstract: As mudanças na distribuição da adequação climática e a variabilidade meteorológica interanual são centrais na reconfiguração da transmissão de doenças tropicais negligenciadas (DTNs) em áreas de borda ecológica. Sintetizam-se aqui evidências sobre a intensificação recente da dengue e a expansão meridional da leishmaniose no Sul do Brasil, examinando a convergência entre adequação ambiental, infraestrutura urbana e conectividade transfronteiriça, na ótica de Saúde Única. Foram verificadas as bases de dados SciELO, Google Scholar e PubMed, utilizando descritores locais e regionais (Cone Sul), para mapear a dinâmica epidemiológica e os modelos de distribuição vetorial até agosto de 2025. Dados espaçotemporais demonstram uma erosão progressiva das barreiras térmicas históricas (invernos frios) no Sul do Brasil, com aumento da infestação por Aedes aegypti e persistência de linhagens virais ao longo do inverno. Esse padrão está acoplado à mobilidade populacional transfronteiriça e à dinâmica climática de outono, em regiões temperadas adjacentes do Cone Sul (Argentina/Uruguai), que exercem pressão bidirecional de importação. Evidências confirmam o avanço meridional de Lutzomyia longipalpis e Migonemyia migonei. Novos desafios operacionais para diagnóstico e vigilância impõem-se. A operacionalização plena da tríade de Saúde Única é fundamental para ampliar a resiliência dos sistemas de saúde e orientar políticas públicas oportunas, interoperáveis e transfronteiriças.

title: Análise de redes complexas na disseminação da dengue no Rio Grande do Norte (2010–2023): Dinâmica espaço-temporal, sazonalidade climática e implicações para a vigilância preditiva Complex network analysis of dengue dissemination in Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil (2010–2023): Spatio-temporal dynamics, climate seasonality, and implications for predictive surveillance Análisis de redes complejas en la diseminación del dengue en Rio Grande do Norte, Brasil (2010–2023): Dinámica espacio-temporal, estacionalidad climática e implicaciones para la vigilancia predictiva
abstract: A dengue permanece como uma das principais arboviroses de impacto epidemiológico no Brasil, com forte associação a determinantes climáticos, urbanos e socioambientais. O presente estudo objetiva propor uma análise aprofundada da disseminação espaço-temporal da dengue no Rio Grande do Norte entre 2010 e 2023, integrando dados epidemiológicos semanais, temperatura, precipitação de chuvas e modelagem por redes complexas. Foram utilizados dados primários provenientes do InfoDengue, INMET e CEMADEN, abrangendo notificações semanais por temperatura e precipitação. A rede foi estruturada a partir de conexões sazonais entre vários municípios do RN, classificando a incidência das notificações dos casos bem como a sincronização temporal dos surtos. Os resultados indicam padrões sazonais recorrentes, com intensificação da transmissão ao final do verão e durante o outono, além de anos atípicos com comportamento epidêmico exacerbado, especialmente 2016 e 2022. A análise revela a existência de semanas epidemiológicas críticas, que requerem ações preventivas antecipadas, como manejo ambiental, limpeza urbana e campanhas focalizadas. O estudo contribui para o avanço de sistemas preditivos baseados em redes epidemiológicas e evidencia o potencial da integração entre ciência de dados, climatologia e saúde pública para entender e atuar na redução do impacto regional da dengue junto aos órgãos públicos.
authors: Marília Gabriela de Azevedo Araújo Santos

title: Comparative Analysis of Hematological, Biochemical, and Inflammatory Biomarkers in Malaria and Dengue Patients in an Endemic Setting of Pakistan
abstract: Abstract Objective To compare the hematological, biochemical, and selected derived inflammatory biomarker profiles of laboratory-confirmed malaria and dengue patients presenting to secondary-care hospitals in District Swat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, and to identify routine laboratory parameters with the greatest potential to support early clinical differentiation of the two infections in resource-constrained endemic settings. Methods A hospital-based comparative cross-sectional study was conducted at the Tehsil Headquarter (THQ) and District Headquarter (DHQ) hospitals of District Swat. Fifty-five malaria and 55 dengue laboratory-confirmed cases were enrolled through consecutive sampling after written informed consent. Hematological parameters (hemoglobin, hematocrit, total white blood cell count, platelet count, neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils), biochemical markers (blood urea, serum creatinine, total bilirubin, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and derived inflammatory indices (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and neutrophil-to-monocyte ratio (NMR) were measured on venous blood drawn at presentation. All analyses were performed in SPSS version 26.0, with a two-sided alpha of 0.05. Results The 110 enrolled patients comprised 55 malaria (mean age 21.76 ± 16.82 years; 58.2% male) and 55 dengue (mean age 31.71 ± 14.41 years; 61.8% male) cases. Dengue patients were significantly older (p = 0.001) and had a marginally higher mean body temperature (102.98 ± 0.76°F vs 102.64 ± 0.95°F; p = 0.037); sex distribution did not differ (p = 0.846). title: Climate-driven dengue forecasting in Bangladesh: division-specific feature-set design and lag structure
abstract: Abstract Bangladesh shows marked annual variation in dengue incidence, partly driven by meteorological effects on Aedes breeding and transmission. We contrast consistently high-burden Dhaka with Barishal, where dengue incidence has recently increased, and emphasize feature-set design and predictor structure as the main methodological contributions. Using monthly dengue data from Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS, 2025 Daily dengue status report) and meteorological data from WorldWeatherOnline (World Weather Online. https://www.worldweatheronline.com/bangladesh-weather.aspx) for January 2022–October 2025, we compare four climate feature sets that vary wetness (rainy days versus rainfall) and sunshine (sun days versus sun hours), with temperature and humidity included in all sets. Correlation analysis across 0–4-month climate lags shows that rainfall has the strongest positive correlations at a 2-month lag, humidity at a 1-month lag, sunshine has the strongest negative correlations at a 2-month lag and temperature shows weak positive correlations at longer lags. For forecasting, we evaluate lagged climate covariates alone and combined with 1-month lagged dengue incidence. We compare multivariate Poisson regression (MPR), artificial neural networks (ANNs), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with eXogenous (SARIMAX) regressors. For Dhaka, ANN-1 with SET-1 performs best (RMSE = 2176.70), whereas for Barishal, SARIMAX((0,1,1)(1,0,0,12)) with SET-2 performs best (RMSE = 817.56). Analyses use consistent monthly aggregation and division-specific tuning.

title: In silico biochemical and structure-based evaluation of Artemisia annua -derived compounds against key dengue hemorrhagic fever molecular targets
abstract: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) continues to be a major public health challenge because of its complicated inflammatory mechanism and lack of an antiviral treatment strategy. The current investigation employs a stringent systems biology approach, including network pharmacology, gene expression studies, and molecular modeling, to identify critical genetic targets in DHF and assess the efficacy of compounds derived from Artemisia annua (A. annua) in treating this condition. Microarray analysis of the GSE18090 and GSE51808 datasets identified differentially expressed genes associated with DHF development. In addition, network pharmacology revealed that artemisinin, luteolin, aurantiamide, and artemisitene can be used to regulate the host inflammatory response by targeting key hub proteins AKT1, HSP90AA1, and ESR1. These proteins play an important role in signaling and stress-related processes in the cell and are often targeted by viruses. The identified interaction was confirmed by molecular docking and a 100-ns MD simulation, which showed a stable complex with high binding affinity. The findings indicated a high binding affinity and structural stability of the compounds within the active sites of their respective targets, with minimal RMSD fluctuations throughout the simulation trajectory. Our results suggest that derivatives of A. annua may alleviate DHF-induced hyperinflammation by targeting multiple proteins. Although these computational insights lay a solid groundwork for drug repurposing, further in vitro and in vivo validation is necessary to verify their efficacy and safety profiles.

source_records.abstract: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) continues to be a major public health challenge because of its complicated inflammatory mechanism and lack of an antiviral treatment strategy. The current investigation employs a stringent systems biology approach, including network pharmacology, gene expression studies, and molecular modeling, to identify critical genetic targets in DHF and assess the efficacy of compounds derived from Artemisia annua (A. annua) in treating this condition. Microarray analysis of the GSE18090 and GSE51808 datasets identified differentially expressed genes associated with DHF development. In addition, network pharmacology revealed that artemisinin, luteolin, aurantiamide, and artemisitene can be used to regulate the host inflammatory response by targeting key hub proteins AKT1, HSP90AA1, and ESR1. These proteins play an important role in signaling and stress-related processes in the cell and are often targeted by viruses. The identified interaction was confirmed by molecular docking and a 100-ns MD simulation, which showed a stable complex with high binding affinity. The findings indicated a high binding affinity and structural stability of the compounds within the active sites of their respective targets, with minimal RMSD fluctuations throughout the simulation trajectory. Our results suggest that derivatives of A. annua may alleviate DHF-induced hyperinflammation by targeting multiple proteins. Although these computational insights lay a solid groundwork for drug repurposing, further in vitro and in vivo validation is necessary to verify their efficacy and safety profiles.

title: Factors associated with dengue prevention behaviors in Southeast Asia: a scoping review
abstract: Background: Dengue prevention in Southeast Asia requires a comprehensive understanding of diverse factors to support context-tailored public health interventions, encompassing both source reduction and personal protection. Objective: This scoping review maps the multidimensional factors (demographic, socioeconomic, psychological, and behavioral) associated with dengue prevention behaviors in Southeast Asia. Methods: Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, this review used a PCC framework with general populations as the population, demographic, socioeconomic, psychological, and behavioral determinants as the concept, and Southeast Asia as the context. Searches across PubMed, Scopus, and ProQuest covered primary studies published from January 1, 2020, to September 11, 2025. Title and abstract screening was initially conducted by one reviewer, followed by independent full-text screening by two reviewers, with data extraction and cross-checking using a standardized charting template. Results: After systematic screening and feasibility assessment of 843 records, we included 16 studies from four countries in the final analysis. The findings indicate that community dengue prevention behaviors were frequently associated with psychological constructs, specifically self-efficacy and cues to action. However, a persistent "knowledge-practice gap" frequently co-occurs alongside socioeconomic and structural barriers, such as income constraints, high-density housing, and unreliable infrastructure, which are inversely associated with routine vector control practices. Conclusion: Because dengue prevention in Southeast Asia is shaped by socio-ecological realities rather than individual choice, future strategies should integrate psychological empowerment with routine breeding-site elimination. Practically, these findings underscore the need for national programs, such as Indonesia’s “1 Rumah 1 Jumantik”, to incorporate psychological approaches to achieve sustainable vector control.

title: Spatial interactions of urban poverty and livestock environments with dengue incidence: A Bivariate Moran's I Analysis in Denpasar, Bali.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) remains a major public health problem in tropical regions, including Indonesia. Its transmission is influenced by complex interactions between environmental, animal, and human factors. This study applies a One Health approach to examine spatial interactions between livestock environments, urban conditions, and dengue incidence in Denpasar, Bali. METHODS This study used a cross-sectional spatial design at the subdistrict level, using secondary data from 2025. Dengue cases were analyzed as the dependent variable, while the number of pig farmers and slum areas represented animal and environmental factors, respectively. Spatial analysis was conducted using QGIS and GeoDa, applying Bivariate Moran's I and BiLISA to identify global and local spatial relationships. RESULTS The analysis showed a significant positive spatial association between the number of pig farmers and dengue incidence (Moran's I = 0.127; p = 0.041), indicating a clustering pattern. Slum areas were not significantly associated with dengue incidence (p = 0.487). Local analysis identified a High-High cluster in Padangsambian Kaja and several Low-High clusters, suggesting potential spatial spillover effects between neighboring areas. DISCUSSION The findings indicate that livestock-related environments may indirectly influence dengue transmission by creating conditions favorable for mosquito breeding. The presence of spatial clustering and spillover effects highlights the importance of considering interregional connectivity and environmental context in disease control strategies. CONCLUSION Dengue distribution in Denpasar is shaped by spatial and environmental dynamics, particularly livestock-related factors. Targeted, spatially informed interventions using a One Health approach are essential to improve the effectiveness of dengue prevention and control.

DISCUSSION The findings indicate that livestock-related environments may indirectly influence dengue transmission by creating conditions favorable for mosquito breeding. The presence of spatial clustering and spillover effects highlights the importance of considering interregional connectivity and environmental context in disease control strategies. CONCLUSION Dengue distribution in Denpasar is shaped by spatial and environmental dynamics, particularly livestock-related factors. Targeted, spatially informed interventions using a One Health approach are essential to improve the effectiveness of dengue prevention and control.

title: MUDANÇAS CLIMÁTICAS, EL NIÑO E DINÂMICA DA DENGUE NA AMÉRICA LATINA: UMA REVISÃO NARRATIVA
abstract: A América Latina apresenta elevada carga de dengue e acentuada vulnerabilidade às mudanças climáticas e ao El Niño-Oscilação Sul (ENSO). Esta revisão narrativa sintetizou as evidências sobre os efeitos das mudanças climáticas, do ENSO e das variáveis meteorológicas na ocorrência e distribuição da dengue e de Aedes aegypti na região. Foram pesquisadas as bases PubMed/MEDLINE, Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde e ScienceDirect até 24 de agosto de 2026. Dos 14 artigos avaliados em texto completo, 12 atenderam aos critérios de elegibilidade. O ENSO influenciou a periodicidade, a sincronização e a intensidade das epidemias, com efeitos defasados entre anomalias oceânicas e aumento dos casos. Temperatura e precipitação estiveram associadas à incidência e à infestação vetorial, porém com relações não lineares e dependentes do contexto. Anomalias térmicas prolongadas e projeções climáticas indicaram expansão da dengue e do vetor para áreas de maior altitude e latitude anteriormente menos adequadas. Urbanização, desigualdade, saneamento, armazenamento de água, mobilidade humana e circulação viral prévia modificaram os efeitos climáticos. Conclui-se que as mudanças climáticas e o ENSO estão alterando as condições temporais e geográficas da transmissão, mas seus efeitos são mediados por características ecológicas e socioambientais. Sistemas de alerta precoce devem integrar indicadores oceânicos, meteorológicos, epidemiológicos, entomológicos e de vulnerabilidade territorial.

title: Pengaruh Pendidikan Kesehatan Menggunakan Media E-Leaflet Terhadap Pengetahuan Dan Sikap Siswa Tentang Demam Berdarah Dengue Di SMKN 16 Samarinda
abstract: Demam Berdarah Dengue (DBD) masih menjadi salah satu masalah kesehatan masyarakat di Indonesia yang dapat menyerang berbagai kelompok usia, termasuk remaja. Rendahnya pengetahuan dan sikap remaja terhadap pencegahan DBD dapat meningkatkan risiko terjadinya penularan penyakit. Salah satu upaya yang dapat dilakukan untuk meningkatkan pemahaman dan membentuk sikap positif remaja adalah melalui pendidikan kesehatan menggunakan media e-leaflet yang mudah diakses, menarik, dan sesuai dengan perkembangan teknologi digital. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh pendidikan kesehatan menggunakan media e-leaflet terhadap pengetahuan dan sikap siswa tentang pencegahan Demam Berdarah Dengue (DBD) di SMKN 16 Samarinda. Penelitian ini menggunakan desain pra-eksperimental dengan pendekatan One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. Populasi penelitian adalah seluruh siswa kelas XI SMKN 16 Samarinda sebanyak 137 siswa. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 64 responden yang dipilih menggunakan teknik proportionate random sampling. Pengumpulan data dilakukan menggunakan kuesioner pengetahuan dan sikap tentang DBD. Data dianalisis menggunakan Uji Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test untuk mengetahui perbedaan sebelum dan sesudah intervensi pendidikan kesehatan menggunakan media e-leaflet. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa terdapat peningkatan pengetahuan dan sikap siswa setelah diberikan pendidikan kesehatan menggunakan media e-leaflet. Analisis statistik menunjukkan adanya perbedaan yang bermakna antara nilai pretest dan posttest pada variabel pengetahuan dan sikap, sehingga media e-leaflet efektif digunakan sebagai sarana edukasi kesehatan mengenai DBD. Pendidikan kesehatan menggunakan media e-leaflet berpengaruh terhadap peningkatan pengetahuan dan sikap siswa tentang pencegahan Demam Berdarah Dengue (DBD) di SMKN 16 Samarinda. Media e-leaflet dapat dijadikan alternatif media promosi kesehatan yang efektif dalam meningkatkan kesadaran dan perilaku pencegahan DBD pada remaja.

title: A dengue sob uma perspectiva epidemiológica e sociodemográfica: uma análise sobre o estado de Minas Gerais
abstract: O contexto epidemiológico da dengue no Brasil caracteriza-se por oscilações entre períodos endêmicos e surtos epidêmicos, representando um desafio contínuo à saúde pública. Este estudo tem como objetivo geral analisar o perfil epidemiológico e sociodemográfico da dengue no estado de Minas Gerais, com ênfase no município de Uberlândia, a partir de evidências da literatura científica recente. Trata-se de uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de caráter descritivo e exploratório, realizada em bases de dados nacionais e internacionais. Os resultados indicam elevada incidência da doença em determinados períodos do ano, forte associação com fatores socioambientais, desigualdades regionais e impacto significativo sobre o Sistema Único de Saúde. Conclui-se que a dengue permanece como um importante problema de saúde pública em Minas Gerais, exigindo estratégias integradas de vigilância epidemiológica, controle vetorial e ações intersetoriais.

title: From laboratory to field: Progress and prospects of the phase conditional approach in two decades of sterile insect technique research against Aedes aegypti in Indonesia.
abstract: Dengue remains a major public health concern in Indonesia, and despite recent progress in vaccine development, vector control remains essential to limit dengue outbreaks and occurrence of clinical cases. Among emerging approaches, the radiation-based sterile insect technique (SIT) has gained attention as an environmentally friendly vector control strategy. This review synthesizes two decades (2004-2024) of SIT research and development against Aedes aegypti in Indonesia, tracing the programme's evolution from unstructured pilot releases to a structured phased conditional approach (PCA) framework that culminated in a recent small-scale field trial in Bandung city. Taking the field trial as the central case study, we identify a core challenge: while SIT can significantly reduce vector populations, suppression remains incomplete and impermanent without optimized integration, as evidenced by post-release population rebound. Further synthesized challenges include navigating the impact of geographical genetic diversity on mating competitiveness, ensuring long-term programme sustainability through stakeholder commitment, and cost-effectiveness concerns for resource-limited settings. To guide the transition toward the pre-operational Phase 3, we propose a dedicated, prioritized research agenda including cluster-randomized controlled trials with entomological and epidemiological endpoints, factorial designs to isolate intervention effects, and development of genetic sexing strains and tailored release protocols, to improve cost-efficiency and prevent population rebound. This synthesis provides a programmatic framework for interpreting Indonesia's SIT development and may inform other dengue-endemic countries considering SIT integration into vector-control programmes.

title: Insecticide resistance in Aedes aegypti across sub-Saharan Africa: An overview and perspectives for effective arbovirus control.
abstract: Arboviruses transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, including Zika, yellow fever and especially dengue and chikungunya, represent a growing public health concern in Africa. Insecticide-based strategies remain essential for the prevention and control of arboviral outbreaks. However, insecticide resistance in Ae. aegypti is globally widespread and appears to be rising in sub-Saharan Africa. Here, we reviewed the distribution and phenotypic and molecular evidence of insecticide resistance in Ae. aegypti across sub-Saharan Africa and summarized the underlying resistance mechanisms and key knowledge gaps. Bibliographic databases were searched for studies published between January 2010 and December 2023. The review identified 40 studies from 18 of 47 countries in sub-Saharan Africa. Among adults mosquitoes, resistance to dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (DDT) and pyrethroids was reported in multiple studies across West and Central Africa, while resistance to carbamates was also documented in several countries, comparatively fewer studies reported resistance to organophosphates. For larvae 7 of 40 studies assessed susceptibility to temephos, with potential resistance reported in only one study. Molecular investigations identified five kdr mutations including F1534C, V1016I, V410L, V1016G and S989P in 12 countries while metabolic resistance involving cytochrome P450s, carboxylesterases, glutathione S-transferases and other detoxification enzymes was reported in a smaller number of studies and countries. Overall, the evidence base remains geographically uneven and limited for several insecticide classes and resistance mechanisms. This review highlights important knowledge gaps, including the limited assessment of larvicides, emerging adulticide options, resistance intensity and Aedes-targeted vector control interventions, and underscores the need for more systematic and standardized insecticide resistance surveillance across sub-Saharan Africa.

This review highlights important knowledge gaps, including the limited assessment of larvicides, emerging adulticide options, resistance intensity and Aedes-targeted vector control interventions, and underscores the need for more systematic and standardized insecticide resistance surveillance across sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Emerging evidence of sand fly fever virus transmission in Sri Lanka
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sand fly fever virus (SFFV) infection is an acute self-limiting febrile illness caused by phleboviruses and transmitted by sand flies of the Phlebotomus species. The disease has been reported in the Mediterranean region, North Africa, the Middle East, and the Indian subcontinent, and is now considered to be expanding into new geographic areas. Clinically, SFFV infection closely resembles acute dengue fever. AIM: To detect other possible infection including SSFV in patients with clinically suspected dengue fever with negative serology results for NS1 antigen. METHODS: In this study, a total of 757 serum samples were collected from patients clinically suspected of dengue fever and admitted to three major hospitals in Sri Lanka between January and August 2023. Patients were from the Colombo and Kandy District, and demographic information was obtained from laboratory request forms, although detailed individual-level demographic data were limited due to anonymization in this laboratory-based study. All samples were initially screened for dengue NS1 antigen negativity and further tested for a panel of pathogens including SFFV immunoglobulin (Ig) M, hantavirus IgM, chikungunya IgM, and leptospira IgM antibodies, as well as molecular detection of hantavirus, flavivirus, and alphavirus RNA. RESULTS: From tested samples, two samples were serologically positive for SFFV-specific IgM using a commercial immunoblot assay, while all other tests for dengue, chikungunya, leptospira, hantavirus, and related RNA viruses were negative. These two SFFV-positive cases were from Kandy District and included one child (6-8 years) and one adult (40-50 years), both presenting with uncomplicated dengue-like illness. CONCLUSION: This study provides the first evidence of SFFV infection in Sri Lanka. Given the high endemicity of dengue in the country, SFFV infections may be clinically misdiagnosed as dengue and therefore remain under-recognized. Further studies involving febrile patients and sand fly vector surveillance are required to determine the true burden and epidemiological significance of SFFV in Sri Lanka.

title: Arboviral risk at Brazilian tourist destinations.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Brazil is a popular travel destination that experiences recurrent outbreaks of dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever (YF), posing a significant health risk to both residents and international travellers. We aimed to identify high-risk regions for arboviral infections and develop a user-friendly, map-based resource to support clinical decision-making in travel medicine. METHODS: We analysed laboratory-confirmed cases and deaths from dengue, chikungunya, and YF reported to Brazil's national surveillance system from 2019 to 2024 (from 2015 for YF). Data were aggregated into 133 Intermediate Geographic Regions (IGRs). IGRs without a confirmed case during the studied period were excluded. A composite risk score was calculated for each IGR by combining (i) transmission duration (months with reported cases per year, score 0-12) and (ii) disease burden, based on national quartiles of monthly incidence and mortality (score 1-4). Annual scores were summed to produce risk maps for each arbovirus. High-risk IGRs (defined as the top quartile of composite score) were overlaid with popular tourist destinations to create an intuitive visual guide. RESULTS: We analysed 4.35 million dengue, 294 921 chikungunya, and 2312 YF cases, resulting in 7846, 565, and 794 deaths, respectively. Dengue affected all IGRs, with high-risk IGRs in the Midwest, including the Pantanal. Chikungunya was also identified in all IGRs, with high-risk IGRs in the Northeast, overlapping with popular beaches such as Recife. YF was identified in 38.3% of IGRs, notably in the Southeast, including São Paulo state. CONCLUSIONS: Arboviruses pose a diverse risk across Brazil. Our spatially integrated map provides a novel tool for travel medicine, enabling healthcare practitioners to offer tailored advice and pre-travel vaccinations to travellers.

title: Influence of environmental, anthropogenic, and climatic changes on vector-borne disease transmission: a comprehensive framework and critical review
abstract: Vector-borne diseases (VBDs) account for more than 17% of all infectious diseases worldwide, causing hundreds of millions of infections and over 700,000 deaths each year. The distribution, intensity, and seasonality of these diseases are profoundly shaped by the interplay of climatic, environmental, and human-driven forces. This manuscript presents a comprehensive, evidence-based framework that integrates three major axes of change: (1) climatic variables—including rising temperatures, altered rainfall patterns, extreme weather events, and El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) cycles; (2) human transformations—encompassing deforestation, agricultural expansion, dam construction, urbanization, globalization, and human mobility; and (3) ecological and environmental disturbances—such as biodiversity loss, habitat fragmentation, and invasive species introductions. Drawing on key findings from literature spanning foundational studies to the most recent publications (up to early 2026), this review examines how these drivers interact to reshape vector competence, pathogen transmission dynamics, and the geographic range of mosquito-, tick-, sandfly-, and other arthropod-borne pathogens — including malaria, dengue, Zika, chikungunya, West Nile virus, Lyme disease, leishmaniasis, and Chagas disease — with particular emphasis on diseases for which robust quantitative evidence exists, while also summarizing the state of knowledge for less studied VBDs. The manuscript further discusses surveillance frameworks, modeling approaches, and integrated One Health adaptation strategies needed to address the growing global burden of VBDs in the context of accelerating planetary change.

title: Development and internal analytical validation of plaque reduction neutralization test for clinical trial application of Kyasanur forest disease virus vaccine.
abstract: Kyasanur Forest Disease (KFD) is a tick-borne viral hemorrhagic fever endemic in the Western Ghats of India. The previous KFD vaccine was discontinued in 2022 due to waning immunity and suboptimal protection. A new vaccine candidate developed by the Indian Council of Medical Research in partnership with Indian Immunologicals Ltd. has progressed to clinical development, necessitating accurate measurement of virus-specific neutralizing antibodies. This study outlines the development, optimization, and internal analytical validation of a plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) for KFD virus using BHK-21 cells, following ICH Q2(R2) guidelines. The acceptance criteria were: assay cut-off (mean + 2SD of negative sera ≤1:10), precision (CV ≤20%), linearity (R2 ≥0.98), and dilution agreement (log10 difference <0.301). Optimized parameters were 5 × 106 cells/well, 1.1% CMC overlay, 72 h incubation, and virus dilution of 10-3·6 TCID50/mL producing 40 ± 5 plaques/well. The virus stock titre was 107·2 TCID50/mL with no significant loss after three freeze-thaw cycles. The assay was evaluated using KFDV-positive (n = 24), heterologous flavivirus-positive (DENV, JEV, WNV, ZIKV; n = 39), and negative sera (n = 107). The operational cutoff based on mean + 2SD was ≥1:10. At ≥1:10 and ≥1:40, the specificity against heterologous flaviviruses sera panel was 61.5% (95% CI 45.9-75.1%) and 100% (95% CI, 91.0-100%) respectively. Inter-assay precision demonstrated CVs of 11.64% and 16.26% for positive controls across two analysts. Linearity was excellent (R2 = 0.998) across 1:10-1:5120. Dilution agreement, tested using four sera at 1:4, 1:16, and 1:64, showed mean recovery of 103.8% (SD 17.3%), with all diluted observations meeting the two-fold criterion. Limitations include requirement of BSL-3 laboratory, modest heterologous sample sizes, single-site validation, and absence of long-term stability studies. The validated PRNT is suitable for measuring vaccine-induced neutralizing antibody responses in clinical trials; broader epidemiological applications would require additional validation.
