source_records.abstract: Kyasanur Forest Disease (KFD) is a tick-borne viral hemorrhagic fever endemic in the Western Ghats of India. The previous KFD vaccine was discontinued in 2022 due to waning immunity and suboptimal protection. A new vaccine candidate developed by the Indian Council of Medical Research in partnership with Indian Immunologicals Ltd. has progressed to clinical development, necessitating accurate measurement of virus-specific neutralizing antibodies. This study outlines the development, optimization, and internal analytical validation of a plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) for KFD virus using BHK-21 cells, following ICH Q2(R2) guidelines. The acceptance criteria were: assay cut-off (mean + 2SD of negative sera ≤1:10), precision (CV ≤20%), linearity (R2 ≥0.98), and dilution agreement (log10 difference <0.301). Optimized parameters were 5 × 106 cells/well, 1.1% CMC overlay, 72 h incubation, and virus dilution of 10-3·6 TCID50/mL producing 40 ± 5 plaques/well. The virus stock titre was 107·2 TCID50/mL with no significant loss after three freeze-thaw cycles. The assay was evaluated using KFDV-positive (n = 24), heterologous flavivirus-positive (DENV, JEV, WNV, ZIKV; n = 39), and negative sera (n = 107). The operational cutoff based on mean + 2SD was ≥1:10. At ≥1:10 and ≥1:40, the specificity against heterologous flaviviruses sera panel was 61.5% (95% CI 45.9-75.1%) and 100% (95% CI, 91.0-100%) respectively. Inter-assay precision demonstrated CVs of 11.64% and 16.26% for positive controls across two analysts. Linearity was excellent (R2 = 0.998) across 1:10-1:5120. Dilution agreement, tested using four sera at 1:4, 1:16, and 1:64, showed mean recovery of 103.8% (SD 17.3%), with all diluted observations meeting the two-fold criterion. Limitations include requirement of BSL-3 laboratory, modest heterologous sample sizes, single-site validation, and absence of long-term stability studies. The validated PRNT is suitable for measuring vaccine-induced neutralizing antibody responses in clinical trials; broader epidemiological applications would require additional validation.

title: Imported mosquito-borne infectious diseases in travellers and migrants: Global patterns, clinical overlap, and prevention gaps-an umbrella review of 21 systematic reviews.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Imported mosquito-borne infectious diseases (MBIDs) pose public health challenges in nonendemic regions, but cross-disease evidence remains fragmented. We conducted an umbrella review of systematic reviews to identify gaps and inform clinical practice and research priorities. METHODS: Five databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library) were searched from inception to December 3, 2025, for systematic reviews on nine imported MBIDs, including chikungunya, dengue, Rift Valley fever, yellow fever, Zika, lymphatic filariasis, malaria, Japanese encephalitis, and West Nile fever. Only English-language publications were included. Epidemiological, clinical, and prevention data were extracted; methodological quality was assessed using AMSTAR 2; and evidence gaps were examined through bibliometric mapping. RESULTS: Of the 2,610 references, 21 systematic reviews were included, resulting in the synthesis of 1,946 studies from 1943 to 2025 across seven of the nine prespecified imported MBIDs. No eligible systematic reviews were identified for Japanese encephalitis or West Nile fever. Dengue had the most importation evidence mainly from Asia, with 42,264 European cases. Malaria had migration flows from West Africa and India. Yellow fever, Rift Valley fever, and lymphatic filariasis were rarely reported, although one migrant-focused review reported 2,449 filariasis cases in Europe. Clinical presentations, particularly fever, myalgia, and rash, overlapped. Severe malaria fatality was 5.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 4.0-6.2%), dengue fatality was 0.08-12.5%, and yellow fever fatality was 28.6%. Only five reviews addressed prevention. The evidence was uneven: 66.4% of the studies were conducted in Europe and 0.6% in Africa; dengue and malaria dominated the output; and Rift Valley fever accounted for <1% of all studies. Methodological quality was critically low in 66.7% of the reviews and high in 9.5%. CONCLUSIONS: The evidence base for imported MBIDs reveals major asymmetries across diseases, outcomes, geographies, and populations, limiting evidence-based management of viral MBIDs, sustaining reliance on symptom-based approaches, and overlooking vulnerable populations.

title: Harnessing Coordinated CD4+ and CD8+ T-Cell Immunity for Virus-Specific Adoptive Immunotherapy in Africa
abstract: Virus-specific T-cell (VST) therapy has developed principally for persistent or reactivating viral infections in immunocompromised patients, with the strongest clinical experience involving cytomegalovirus, Epstein–Barr virus, human adenovirus, BK polyomavirus and human herpesvirus 6. Whether this approach can be extended to emerging and re-emerging viral infections remains less certain. Evidence that virus-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells contribute to natural or vaccine-induced protection provides a biological basis for therapeutic development but does not establish the efficacy of adoptively transferred VSTs. This distinction is particularly important for viruses of relevance to Africa, including Ebola virus, Lassa virus, Marburg virus, dengue virus, chikungunya virus, Rift Valley fever virus and mpox virus. Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) provides clinical proof-of-concept that rapidly developed, partially HLA-matched or banked virus-reactive T-cell products can be administered against a newly emerging pathogen. Experimental adoptive transfer studies provide additional evidence for selected pathogens, including Ebola virus, whereas other emerging viruses remain supported mainly by human immunological, epitope or preclinical data. Translation to African populations will require definition of protective viral targets, population-relevant HLA restrictions, viral sequence conservation, manufacturing feasibility and clinical indications in which cellular therapy offers a clear advantage. This review examines the evidence required to move from antiviral T-cell immunity to therapeutic VST development and proposes a framework for evaluating emerging and re-emerging viral infections as future VST targets in Africa.
journal: Journal of Clinical Care and Medical Advancement

title: Dehydration in Tropical Fevers: Rethinking Fluid and Electrolyte Replacement
abstract: Tropical fevers, including dengue, malaria, typhoid, chikungunya, leptospirosis, and scrub typhus, impose a substantial and growing public health burden in the tropical and subtropical regions, particularly the Indian subcontinent.Climate change, monsoon season, and inadequate sanitation further exacerbate transmission dynamics and outbreak patterns.Dehydration represents a critical yet frequently underrecognized complication of these infections.It is attributed to high-grade fever, vomiting, excessive sweating, decreased oral intake, and pathophysiological mechanisms, such as plasma leakage in dengue, hemolysis in malaria, and gastrointestinal losses in typhoid.Electrolyte disturbances, specifically hyponatremia, hypokalemia, and hypochloremia, contribute to the severity of these conditions and likelihood of multiorgan failure.Inadequate hydration amplifies underlying physiological dysfunction, including hemoconcentration, hypovolemic shock, acute kidney injury, and cardiovascular compromise, thereby increasing hospitalization rates, morbidity, and mortality.This review explores the disease-specific hydration challenges across diverse tropical fevers and evaluates the current strategies for effective fluid management.The World Health Organization (WHO), United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund (UNICEF), and national guidelines recommend oral rehydration therapy, formulated with optimized sodium and glucose concentrations to promote rehydration through facilitation of the intestinal sodiumglucose co-transporter (SGLT1) mechanism for management of ambulatory and mild-to-moderate cases.Its efficacy in symptom relief, minimizing intravenous fluid requirements, and accelerating clinical recovery is well established.However, individualized and careful calibration of fluid management remains essential to prevent fluid overload and other related complications.Thus, integrating standardized, evidence-based hydration protocols into routine clinical practice holds the potential to be a practical and cost-effective strategy for managing tropical infection in India and other regions with similar climatic and epidemiological settings.

subtropical regions, particularly the Indian subcontinent.Climate change, monsoon season, and inadequate sanitation further exacerbate transmission dynamics and outbreak patterns.Dehydration represents a critical yet frequently underrecognized complication of these infections.It is attributed to high-grade fever, vomiting, excessive sweating, decreased oral intake, and pathophysiological mechanisms, such as plasma leakage in dengue, hemolysis in malaria, and gastrointestinal losses in typhoid.Electrolyte disturbances, specifically hyponatremia, hypokalemia, and hypochloremia, contribute to the severity of these conditions and likelihood of multiorgan failure.Inadequate hydration amplifies underlying physiological dysfunction, including hemoconcentration, hypovolemic shock, acute kidney injury, and cardiovascular compromise, thereby increasing hospitalization rates, morbidity, and mortality.This review explores the disease-specific hydration challenges across diverse tropical fevers and evaluates the current strategies for effective fluid management.The World Health Organization (WHO), United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund (UNICEF), and national guidelines recommend oral rehydration therapy, formulated with optimized sodium and glucose concentrations to promote rehydration through facilitation of the intestinal sodiumglucose co-transporter (SGLT1) mechanism for management of ambulatory and mild-to-moderate cases.Its efficacy in symptom relief, minimizing intravenous fluid requirements, and accelerating clinical recovery is well established.However, individualized and careful calibration of fluid management remains essential to prevent fluid overload and other related complications.Thus, integrating standardized, evidence-based hydration protocols into routine clinical practice holds the potential to be a practical and cost-effective strategy for managing tropical infection in India and other regions with similar climatic and epidemiological settings.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Rapid Diagnostic Tests Versus Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) Across Major Infectious Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) are increasingly used for point-of-care diagnosis of infectious diseases because of their rapid turnaround time and ease of use.However, their diagnostic performance compared with enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) varies across diseases and assay platforms.This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines.A total of 26 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, of which 13 datasets from 11 studies with complete 2 × 2 diagnostic data were included in the meta-analysis.Quality assessment was performed using QUADAS-2 (Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2).Pooled diagnostic performance was summarized separately for each infection using extracted true-positive (TP), false-positive (FP), true-negative (TN), and false-negative (FN) values; forest plots, an HSROC (Hierarchical Summary Receiver Operating Characteristic model)-style summary visualization, and a Deeks-type funnel plot were generated.The aggregate diagnostic counts were TP = 1,304, FP = 68, TN = 24,301, and FN = 303.Overall, the included datasets showed consistently high specificity (≥96.97%),whereas sensitivity varied widely (25%-100%) across conditions.By target condition, the pooled sensitivity and specificity were human immunodeficiency virus (HIV; 78.6%/99.30%),hepatitis B virus (HBV; 88.2%/99.94%),hepatitis C virus (HCV; 75.7%/99.42%),dengue (97.0%/99.97%),and malaria (100.0%/97.18%).RDTs demonstrated high specificity and good sensitivity compared with ELISA, supporting their role as rapid screening tools, particularly in resource-limited settings.However, heterogeneity across diseases and assay platforms limits generalizability, and confirmatory testing remains important in selected clinical and blood-screening settings.

title: Climate Change and Health Vulnerability in Korail and Rayer Bazar Slums, Dhaka, Bangladesh
abstract: Abstract Urbanization is accelerating, and climate change is becoming more severe, endangering environmental health in Dhaka's informal settlements, leaving communities such as Korail and Rayer Bazar particularly vulnerable to current and future threats. The aim of this study is to assess the climate-related health vulnerability in the Korail and Rayer Bazar slums and highlight how climate risks, environmental deprivation, socioeconomic vulnerability, and adaptive capacity interact to shape health risks in the Korail and Rayer Bazar slums in Dhaka. Relevant literature was searched in Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect. The time range of the articles searched in the databases ranged from 2002 to 2026. The review highlights the primary exposure pathways from climate change to increased risk of diarrheal disease, dengue and other vector-borne diseases, respiratory illness, cardiovascular strain, heat-related illness, social and psychological distress, and delayed healthcare seeking. Important differences were identified in these two settlements. Korail is comparatively better in terms of evidence, use of NGO services, and improved infrastructure support, but Rayer Bazaar has fewer climate-health research studies and is more dependent on informal coping mechanisms. Extreme climate hazards and a lack of water, sanitation, and hygiene infrastructure, combined with precarious socioeconomic conditions, create a disproportionately high health burden in Korail and Rayer Bazar that needs to be addressed through systemic urban upgrading and integrated vector management, both of which are essential to climate resilience.

title: How accurate are effective reproduction number estimates for mosquito-borne diseases in urban settings?
abstract: The time-varying effective reproduction number, Rt, characterizes the dynamics of infectious disease transmission at a given point in time. For mosquito-borne diseases, there has been growing interest in estimating Rt for spatially targeted vector control interventions. However, systematic evaluations of Rt estimation accuracy for mosquito-borne diseases are lacking: a concerning phenomenon given that errors in Rt estimation at fine spatial scales could be amplified by human mobility-driven transmission and high rates of asymptomatic cases. We systematically evaluated the accuracy of popular Rt estimation tools, EpiEstim and EpiFilter, against ground truth transmission pair data generated by agent-based simulations of dengue epidemics involving humans and mosquitoes in Singapore. We applied data collection artefacts to simulate real-world operational challenges, including spatial and temporal aggregation of incidence data, under-reporting of cases and reporting delays. The findings suggest that EpiEstim and EpiFilter are not well-suited for estimating Rt for mosquito-borne diseases at fine spatial scales because they assume localized disease transmission, whereas human mobility is a significant driver of transmission across wider geographic scales. Consequently, public health officials should be cautious when interpreting Rt estimates at fine spatial scales. Our findings highlight an urgent need for innovations in Rt estimation tools for mosquito-borne diseases.
journal: Journal of the Royal Society, Interface

title: Unveiling the Phytoconstituents and Health Benefits of Carica papaya L.: From Traditional Medicine to Modern Therapeutics.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The tropical plant Carica papaya L., which is a member of the Caricaceae family, is well known for its medicinal and nutritional qualities. The plant's leaves, fruits, seeds, and latex have all historically been used to treat inflammatory diseases, cancer, metabolic abnormalities, and infections. The objective of this review is to provide a thorough overview of the phytochemical composition, pharmacological activity, mechanisms of action, and clinical evidence that support its potential for therapeutic use. METHODS: Based on a thorough evaluation of the literature, this work is a narrative review. Electronic databases such as PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were used to conduct a thorough search. Based on predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria, pertinent peer-reviewed publications, including experimental research, clinical trials, and ethnomedical reports, were selected. The following keywords were used: phytochemistry, pharmacological activity, mechanisms of action, and Carica papaya. An integrative assessment of its therapeutic potential was produced by rigorously analysing and synthesizing the extracted data. RESULTS: Alkaloids (carpaine), flavonoids (quercetin, kaempferol), phenolic acids, and enzymes (papain, chymopapain) are among the many bioactive substances found in Carica papaya. These substances have a variety of pharmacological actions, such as immunomodulatory, antiinflammatory, antioxidant, anticancer, antibacterial, and antidiabetic properties. Mechanistically, they reduce oxidative stress and inflammation by modulating important molecular pathways such as NF-κB, MAPK, and COX-2. Clinical research indicates that leaf extracts may have positive effects, especially in dengue-associated thrombocytopenia. High-dose seed extracts, however, could be harmful. DISCUSSION: Carica papaya's extensive phytochemical profile and capacity to control important molecular pathways involved in oxidative stress and inflammation are responsible for the vast range of pharmacological activity seen in this plant. Its promise as a therapeutic agent is highlighted by the merging of ancient knowledge with contemporary pharmacological research, particularly in infectious and inflammatory illnesses. CONCLUSION: Carica papaya shows great promise as a nutraceutical and phytotherapeutic agent. Even though there is encouraging experimental and clinical evidence, more carefully planned research is needed to determine uniform dosages, long-term safety, and clinical efficacy for its wider therapeutic application.
journal: Recent advances in food, nutrition & agriculture

title: FEATURES OF THE OPERATION OF EPIDEMIOLOGICAL SURVEILLANCE SYSTEMS IN THE CONTEXT OF CLIMATE CHANGE. AN ANALYSIS OF INTERNATIONAL EXPERIENCE
abstract: To analyze the challenges faced by Ukraine’s epidemiological surveillance system as a result of climate change over the past decade and to systematize international experience in adapting epidemic control measures, infection prevention and control, and biosafety practices to high-temperature environments. MATERIALS AND METHODS. Content analysis of scientific publications from databases, regulatory documents, and WHO recommendations concerning the functioning of healthcare facilities and laboratories in hot regions. Climate change impacts the dynamics of vector-borne, enteric, and zoonotic infections. A reduction in the extrinsic incubation period in vectors (Culex, Aedes, Ixodidae) accelerates the transmission of vector-borne infections, including West Nile fever, dengue, and malaria. Prolonged periods spent in air-conditioned indoor environments during heatwaves increase the risk of respiratory pathogen transmission. In healthcare facilities, high temperatures promote biofilm formation, accelerate disinfectant degradation, and create optimal conditions for the proliferation of opportunistic pathogens (Legionella spp., Pseudomonas aeruginosa). Working in personal protective equipment (PPE) under hot conditions can cause heat stress and impair cognitive-motor functions, thereby increasing the risk of biosafety breaches during PPE removal (doffing). The vulnerability of the cold chain for immunobiological medicinal products and reagents during transport is also underlined. Under climate change conditions, transforming the country's current surveillance framework toward Integrated Disease Surveillance by incorporating meteorological indicators into Early Warning Systems is highly relevant. Protection modernization requires revising standard operating procedures (SOPs) for disinfection and WASH infrastructure, regulating working conditions for personnel wearing PPE, equipping epidemiological response teams with temperature-monitoring devices, and conducting risk communication training regarding public health threats.

title: Impact of fever in pregnancy on maternal and fetal outcomes: a prospective observational study of 171 cases
abstract: Background: Fever during pregnancy is a high-risk condition associated with adverse fetomaternal outcomes; however, region-specific data from Indian tertiary care government hospitals remain limited. This study evaluated fetomaternal outcomes and etiological spectrum of fever in pregnancy. Methods: This prospective observational study was conducted over 18 months in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology of a tertiary care government hospital. Total 171 pregnant women with oral/axillary temperature ≥38°C were enrolled after informed consent. Demographic, obstetric, fever-related variables were recorded, maternal and neonatal outcomes were followed until 6weeks postpartum. Data were analysed using SPSS with chi-square/Fisher exact test; p<0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: Most women were aged 21-35 years (91.2%) and multigravida (52.0%). Fever occurred predominantly in second trimester (43.3%) and was low-to-moderate grade (94.7%). Urinary tract infection (23.4%), typhoid fever (14.6%), upper respiratory tract infection (13.4%) were commonest causes. title: Factors Influencing Acceptance of Ricinus communis L. Natural Larvicides
abstract: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, particularly in Medan City, North Sumatra. As the effectiveness of chemical larvicides continues to decline, there is growing interest in natural, eco-friendly alternatives such as larvicides derived from castor seeds (Ricinus communis L.). This study aims to examine the factors influencing the acceptance of these natural larvicides among housewives in Medan City. A cross-sectional design was used, involving 844 respondents across 21 districts. The analysis was carried out in four stages: univariate analysis to describe respondent characteristics, chi-square tests for bivariate relationships, logistic regression for multivariate assessment, and spatial analysis to identify geographic patterns of larvicide acceptance. The findings reveal that demographic variables such as age, education, and dengue history do not significantly affect acceptance. However, the relationship between attitude and knowledge and the acceptance of dengue prevention measures statistically significant. In addition, attitude was the most dominant independent factor in predicting the acceptance of Ricinus communis L. natural larvicide as a measure to prevent dengue fever in logistic regression (OR = 3.624; p < 0.001). This indicates that internal readiness and positive perceptions play a crucial role in encouraging the acceptance of eco-friendly larvicide options.

title: Scrub Typhus with Multiple Organ Dysfunction and Thrombocytopenia – A Case Study
abstract: Background: Scrub typhus is an acute zoonotic infection caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi and may progress to thrombocytopenia and multiple organ dysfunction. Case Presentation: A 57-year-old man presented with a one-week history of fever, cough with expectoration, headache, and dyspnoea. At admission, he was unconscious. Investigations showed severe thrombocytopenia, raised creatinine, hepatic dysfunction, encephalopathy, and acute kidney injury. Testing for scrub typhus was positive, while dengue and malaria markers were negative. During hospitalisation, the patient developed worsening respiratory status, decreased urine output, recurrent atrial fibrillation, septic shock, and multiple organ dysfunction. Bi-level positive airway pressure was initiated, followed by intubation and mechanical ventilation when respiratory status failed to improve. Doxycycline was added to the treatment regimen, with azithromycin and rifaximin also administered. Supportive management included intravenous antibiotics, fluids, inotropes, respiratory support, cardiovascular management, and continued monitoring. The patient subsequently improved, was extubated, and transferred from the intensive care unit to the ward. Platelet count increased, C-reactive protein decreased, acute kidney injury resolved, and liver function showed recovery. At discharge, the patient was clinically improved, haemodynamically stable, with improving sensorium and recovered renal and hepatic functions. Conclusion: This case demonstrates the severe multisystem presentation of scrub typhus with thrombocytopenia and emphasises the importance of timely diagnosis, antimicrobial therapy, and supportive care.

title: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics of virus-host interactions: from systems to structure
abstract: This thesis investigates viral infection across multiple levels of biological organization using mass spectrometry-based proteomics, complemented by other approaches. Viral infections are inherently complex and involve coordinated interactions between viral factors and the host, ranging from systemic responses, to intracellular signaling, antigen structure, innate and adaptive immunity. To capture this complexity, the thesis integrates plasma proteomics, phosphoproteomics, glycoproteomics, and methodological advances in de novo antibody sequencing, together with cryo-EM and live-cell microscopy. Chapter 1 of the thesis establishes the biological and analytical background, introducing key aspects of viral biology, host responses to infection, and the application of mass spectrometry-based proteomics in virology. Chapter 2 addresses the systemic host response to dengue virus infection through high-throughput plasma proteomics of a large pediatric cohort. By comparing subclinical infection, dengue fever, and severe dengue across multiple disease phases, this work demonstrates that circulating proteins capture immune activation, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and disease progression. These results show that plasma is a powerful source of information on host physiology during infection and may support biomarker discovery for disease severity and patient stratification. Chapter 3 focuses on intracellular signaling during Ebola virus replication using bottom-up proteomics, phosphoproteomics, and microscopy. This work reveals extensive rewiring of kinase-driven signaling pathways, particularly involving cyclin-dependent kinases, and shows that Ebola virus replication drives cells toward an S/G2-like state to support replication and transcription. Functional validation with small-molecule inhibitors demonstrates how phosphoproteomics can identify host-directed therapeutic targets. Chapter 4 investigates the structural characterization of cetacean coronavirus spike proteins through an integrative approach of cryo-EM and glycoproteomics. Cryo-EM resolved the overall architecture of the spike proteins, while glycoproteomics revealed glycan composition at site-specific resolution. In addition to canonical N-linked glycosylation, extended O-glycosylated regions were identified, showing that viral glycosylation can be more heterogeneous and less predictable than previously recognized. These findings have important implications for antigen structure, host adaptation and immune recognition. Chapter 5 introduces methodological advances in de novo antibody sequencing. By combining HTA proteases with optimized hybrid mass spectrometric acquisition strategies, this work improves sequence coverage and increases the robustness of antibody sequence reconstruction. The resulting workflows provide a basis for future studies of antibody responses to viral infection and immune profiling. Chapter 6 integrates the findings of the thesis and places them in the context of current virology and proteomics research. A central conclusion is that viral infection is best understood through integrative analytical strategies. Across all chapters, viruses were found to consistently reshape the host environment. At the same time, many viruses converge on hijacking a limited set of host pathways, including cytoskeleton organization, translation, cell cycle regulation, DNA damage response, RNA metabolism, and immune signaling. This supports the concept of pan-viral host dependencies and suggests that shared host pathways may represent promising targets for broad-spectrum antiviral strategies. Overall, this thesis demonstrates that mass spectrometry-based proteomics provides a powerful and versatile strategy to study viral infections. When integrated with structural biology and imaging, proteomics enables a multidimensional understanding of virus-host interactions, from organism-level responses to molecular mechanisms.

Chapter 6 integrates the findings of the thesis and places them in the context of current virology and proteomics research. A central conclusion is that viral infection is best understood through integrative analytical strategies. Across all chapters, viruses were found to consistently reshape the host environment. At the same time, many viruses converge on hijacking a limited set of host pathways, including cytoskeleton organization, translation, cell cycle regulation, DNA damage response, RNA metabolism, and immune signaling. This supports the concept of pan-viral host dependencies and suggests that shared host pathways may represent promising targets for broad-spectrum antiviral strategies. Overall, this thesis demonstrates that mass spectrometry-based proteomics provides a powerful and versatile strategy to study viral infections. When integrated with structural biology and imaging, proteomics enables a multidimensional understanding of virus-host interactions, from organism-level responses to molecular mechanisms.

title: Clinical Mimickers of Mpox: A Case Series from a Tropical Referral Center
abstract: Mpox is a zoonotic disease caused by the monkeypox virus, a double-stranded DNA virus belonging to the genus Orthopoxvirus. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared mpox a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) in July 2022 amid the global clade IIb outbreak and again in August 2024 following an increase in cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo associated with clades Ia and Ib. Despite increased awareness, diagnosing mpox remains challenging because its clinical manifestations often overlap with those of other infectious and non-infectious conditions. This diagnostic challenge occurs across geographic settings but may be further complicated in tropical regions by the circulation of locally prevalent infections, including arboviral diseases such as dengue and chikungunya. Here, we describe a series of nine patients initially evaluated for suspected mpox, in whom alternative diagnoses were subsequently established.

title: West Nile Fever in Brazil in 2026: Emergence of Human Cases and Implications for Integrated Surveillance
abstract: West Nile fever (WNF) is a zoonotic arboviral disease caused by West Nile virus (WNV), maintained primarily in an enzootic cycle involving birds and mosquitoes, particularly species of the genus Culex. Although evidence of viral circulation has previously been documented in Brazil, human disease remains infrequently recognized. This study aimed to describe the human cases of WNF identified in Brazil in 2026 and to interpret their epidemiological significance within an integrated One Health surveillance framework. A descriptive retrospective study was conducted using secondary information from the Ministry of Health, state and municipal health authorities, scientific literature, and official technical documents, incorporating information available through 28 August 2026. Four human cases were confirmed—two in Santa Catarina and two in São Paulo—and one probable/under-investigation case was identified in Piauí. The confirmed cases showed heterogeneous clinical presentations, including neuroinvasive manifestations, hospitalization, and one death; the latter was recorded as associated with stroke, with its relationship to WNV infection remaining under investigation. One confirmed case had recent travel to the Amazon region, while other probable sites of infection remained under investigation. The available public sources did not provide concurrent entomological or animal surveillance results sufficient to establish a local transmission chain. The 2026 events therefore constitute a sentinel epidemiological signal that supports intensification of integrated human, laboratory, entomological, animal, and environmental surveillance rather than inference of sustained autochthonous transmission.

title: Identification of Novel Inhibitors of JEV RdRp as Potent Antiviral Drugs: Targeting NS5-NS3 Protein Interaction
abstract: Japanese Encephalitis Virus (JEV) belongs to the Flavivirus family, and the RNA dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) domain located at the C terminus of non structural protein 5 (NS5) regulates de novo viral genome synthesis. The conserved priming loop inserted in the thumb domain of RDRP initiates de novo genome synthesis. Interestingly, the reported replication process initiates with an interaction between NS5 (methyltransferase/RDRP) and NS3 (protease/helicase), and inhibiting this interaction directly correlates with the inhibition of viral replication. The function of the priming loop in the context of the NS5 NS3 interaction is not yet known. In this study, we studied the priming loop function in the NS5 NS3 interaction and viral replication. Using a structure based drug design approach, we screened the Maybridge compound library against the RdRp priming loop and identified 15 candidate compounds based on binding energy. Among them, DSHS00151 showed significant dose dependent inhibition of the NS5 NS3 interaction with an IC50 of 3.5 micromolar in the mammalian two hybrid assay, inhibited viral infectivity with an IC50 of 2.54 micromolar, and reduced viral RNA load with an IC50 of 2.9 micromolar, compared to CD10712. Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that DSHS00151 exhibits stronger and more stable binding with the priming loop residues (790 to 812) compared to CD10712. The molecular mechanism suggested by the docking of the NS5 and NS3 proteins showed that the priming loop tends to rotate toward the NS3 protein to stabilize the complex, and compound binding restricts this loop rotation, thus compromising the stability of the NS5 and NS3 complex and affecting viral replication. Overall, our study validated the function of the NS5 priming loop as an allosteric site, and compounds binding to this allosteric site belong to the Non Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NNRTI) class of inhibitors, which disrupt the NS5 and NS3 interaction and could be developed as novel anti JEV therapeutics.

title: Interferon gamma and inflammatory response genes by weighted gene co-expression network analysis reveal significant associations with severe dengue infection in India
abstract: Objective Dengue virus, with four serotypes (DENV 1-4), is transmitted by Aedes aegypti . India carries 34% of global cases, yet studies to understand how the immune system reacts to dengue infection remain limited. Design This study uncovers early transcriptional signatures from whole blood of 112 NS1 positive hospital reported dengue patients and dissect biological processes linked to varying disease severities “with (WS ) and without (-WS ) warning signs”. Results Differential gene expression analysis showed suppressed innate response in WS patients, with downregulated cytokines ( CXCL8, CXCL16, CXCL2, IL1B) and disrupted platelet function. Upregulation was observed in genes related to glycosylation, nervous system, and metabolism. WGCNA module-trait analysis identified interferon response and inflammation as positively correlated with platelet count, highlighting key genes, IFI44L , IFI35 , OAS1 , HERC6 and SAMDL9 contributing to comparative severe outcomes. CTTN involved in maintenance of vascular permeability showed highest significant association with low platelet count. abstract_zh: 目的 登革病毒病毒具有四个血清型(DENV 1-4),通过Aedes aegypti传播。印度占全球病例的34%,但关于登革病毒感染如何引发免疫应答的研究仍较为有限。设计 本研究分析了112例医院报告的NS1阳性登革热患者的全血早期转录组特征,并解析了与不同疾病严重程度相关的生物过程,包括有(WS)和无(-WS)预警信号的情况。结果 差异基因表达分析显示,WS患者的先天免疫应答受到抑制,细胞因子(CXCL8、CXCL16、CXCL2、IL1B)下调,血小板功能紊乱。与之相反,与糖基化、神经系统和代谢相关的基因表达上调。WGCNA模块-表型分析发现,干扰素反应和炎症与血小板计数呈正相关,突出了关键基因IFI44L、IFI35、OAS1、HERC6和SAMDL9在相对严重疾病结果中的作用。参与维持血管通透性的CTTN基因与低血小板计数显示出最高显著关联。IFI44L成为显著标志物,其在血小板计数低于100 × 10ˆ9/L的患者与血小板计数在100-140 × 10ˆ9/L之间的患者之间表现出最高的转录计数差异。结论 本研究推进了对登革病毒感染的理解,并在感染初期识别了可能的临床生物标志物。这些发现可能有助于改善登革病毒感染的诊断和治疗策略。

full_text: Abstract Climate change is increasingly affecting the transmission dynamics of climate-sensitive infectious diseases, particularly in rapidly urbanizing tropical regions. Jakarta serves as a pertinent case study due to its high population density, complex urban environment, and exposure to climate variability, all of which contribute to persistent dengue transmission. In 2024, Indonesia reported over 210,000 dengue fever cases and 1,239 deaths, with approximately 12,000 cases in Jakarta by September and continued transmission into early 2025. Although dengue surveillance in Jakarta is well established through a provincial web-based reporting system, climate and health data are managed through separate institutional processes. This separation limits public health authorities’ ability to interpret epidemiological patterns within their environmental context and to identify potential high-risk periods. This study describes the design and implementation of a climate-informed surveillance dashboard within the District Health Information System 2 (DHIS2) platform. Monthly dengue surveillance data from the Jakarta Provincial Health Office were combined with meteorological indicators from the Indonesian Meteorological, Climatological, and Geophysical Agency, including rainfall, temperature, humidity, and wind speed. Climate indicators were preprocessed and incorporated into DHIS2 as structured variables, enabling joint visualization and descriptive analysis alongside dengue surveillance data. The implementation demonstrates the feasibility of integrating climate indicators into routine surveillance dashboards. Integrating environmental data into existing health information systems enables surveillance officers to interpret dengue trends within their environmental context, thereby facilitating more informed situational awareness in urban public health monitoring. Identifying influential actors is essential for public health communication, yet existing social network analysis relies on text and ignores visual signals such as video thumbnails. This study proposes a multimodal framework based on Adaptive Gated Fusion that combines text and visual features without any audio modality. Textual features from IndoBERT and visual features from ResNet-50 are fused adaptively per dimension, aggregated per channel, and used to build a content-based co-audience network analysed with PageRank. Using 33,233 Indonesian comments from 5,365 videos across 1,129 collected channels (1,084 retained after language filtering) over 2021 to 2025, an ablation study with stratified five-fold cross-validation shows the fused representation reaches 79.52 percent accuracy and 78.42 percent macro F1, outperforming text and visual baselines. Keywords: Adaptive gated fusion, Co-audience graph, Dengue haemorrhagic fever, IndoBERT, PageRank, ResNet- 50, Sentiment analysis, Social network analysis, YouTube. 1. Introduction Dengue haemorrhagic fever (DHF) is a tropical infectious disease transmitted through the bites of the Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes, and it is one of the major public health burdens in Indonesia. The World Health Organization (WHO) recorded 149,866 confirmed DHF cases in Indonesia up to 1 July 2024, an increase of roughly threefold compared with the same period in 2023, spread across 465 regencies/cities in 38 provinces [1]. Although the case trend declined in 2025, DHF remains a health priority that requires effective prevention strategies and public education [2]. As case numbers rise, the Indonesian public increasingly relies on social media as a source of health information. YouTube has a unique characteristic as a multimodal platform: its content combines visual elements in the form of video thumbnails and textual elements in the form of user comments, which jointly shape public health perceptions and behaviour [3]. However, the openness of this platform also presents challenges, because the information that circulates is not always accurate and can negatively affect public health decisions [4]. Identifying the most influential actors in the dissemination of DHF information is crucial for designing well-targeted interventions. Social Network Analysis (SNA) has proven effective for this purpose: centrality metrics such as PageRank, degree centrality, and betweenness centrality are widely used to measure the level of influence of a node in a network [5], while community detection through the Louvain algorithm enables actors to be grouped according to similar interaction patterns [6]. However, previous research applying SNA to health information has been dominated by text-based platforms such as Twitter and Facebook [7]. As a result, when influence is measured solely from textual signals, the visual dimension that also Received: June 18, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 669 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.34 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ determines the reach of content, particularly thumbnails on platforms such as YouTube, is entirely overlooked. On multimodal platforms, measuring influence from text alone risks misjudging which actors shape public discourse, so a representation capable of capturing both modalities simultaneously is needed. In natural language processing, pre-trained transformer-based models such as BERT have transformed the way text is represented, and IndoBERT in particular is able to understand the context of the Indonesian language better than multilingual models [8]; this capability has been exploited for sentiment analysis of YouTube comments [9] and emotion classification [10]. In computer vision, ResNet-50 is a deep learning architecture widely used for visual feature extraction because its residual learning approach enables the construction of deep networks with effective training [11]. Multimodal approaches that fuse textual and visual features have been shown to improve analytical accuracy compared with unimodal approaches [12]. In particular, the Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF) technique combines the two modalities through a gating mechanism that assigns dynamic per-dimension weights between text and visual features [13], so that the contribution of each modality is not set uniformly but is adjusted to the characteristics of each piece of content. AGF therefore has the potential to address the limitations of text-based analysis by integrating the visual signals that have so far been ignored in identifying influential actors on multimodal platforms. Based on the review above, two main gaps can be identified. First, studies on influential actors in health information still focus on text-based platforms, whereas YouTube, which combines text and visuals, has not been widely studied. Second, SNA research generally still uses only a single type of data, so the visual information in video content has not been optimally exploited; in particular, the combination of IndoBERT and ResNet-50 through adaptive fusion to build a co-audience network has never been explored. To address these gaps, this study proposes an AGF- based multimodal framework for identifying influential actors in the dissemination of DHF information on YouTube. The main objectives of this study are described as follows: 1. Multimodal Representation: integrating IndoBERT textual embeddings and ResNet-50 visual embeddings through Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF), which assigns adaptive per- dimension weights across modalities, without relying on the audio modality. 2. Network Construction: building a co-audience graph based on multimodal content similarity derived from AGF, rather than explicit interactions, and applying PageRank-based SNA to identify influential channels together with their community structure. 3. Sentiment Profiling: fine-tuning a RoBERTa model for Indonesian text to build sentiment profiles for each influential channel. 4. Empirical Validation: conducting an ablation study with stratified 5-fold cross-validation on seven modality configurations to evaluate whether the adaptively fused multimodal representation outperforms the unimodal text and visual baselines in sentiment classification accuracy. The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 reviews related works on multimodal sentiment analysis, social network analysis, and sentiment analysis of health content. Section 3 describes the dataset and the proposed AGF-based multimodal framework. Section 4 presents the experimental results and discussion. Finally, Section 5 concludes the paper and outlines directions for future work. 2. Related works 2.1 Multimodal sentiment analysis Multimodal sentiment analysis combines information from several modalities, typically text, audio, and visual, to produce a richer representation than a single modality alone. Gandhi et al. [14] concluded that multimodal fusion methods outperform unimodal approaches across various datasets, and Zhu et al. [15] reinforced this finding through a survey of fusion methods that emphasised that selecting the appropriate fusion strategy is highly decisive for model performance. In a domain similar to this study, Kothuri and RajaLakshmi [16] proposed the MALO-LSTM model, which combines text, audio, and visual modalities for sentiment analysis on YouTube; the model achieved 98.62% accuracy and showed that combining the three modalities yields better results than using the modalities separately. Recent research emphasises the importance of adaptive fusion mechanisms, that is, mechanisms that adjust the weight of each modality according to context. Wang et al. [17] proposed a multimodal transformer that assigns modality weights adaptively, whereas Lu et al. [18] developed a gated-fusion- based framework that has been shown to filter signals across modalities through a sigmoid gate that dynamically determines the magnitude of each Received: June 18, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 670 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.34 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ modality's contribution [19]. However, most of these methods were developed for English-language data and still rely on the audio modality, so the potential of the visual modality in the form of thumbnails, the primary signal on platforms such as YouTube, has not been optimally exploited, particularly for Indonesian-language content. 2.2 Social network analysis for influential actor identification Social Network Analysis (SNA) is widely used to identify key actors in online information networks. The PageRank algorithm, originally designed to rank web pages [20] was later adapted to the social network context, measuring the influence of a node not only from the number of connections but also from their quality. Rashidi et al. [21] developed a method to predict influential nodes based on local communities and user reaction information, and the results showed that nodes with high PageRank values tend to be effective information spreaders. Similarly, data-driven frameworks combine several centrality metrics such as degree centrality, betweenness centrality, and PageRank to make node rankings more accurate [22]. In the health context, identifying influential actors is highly important for designing public communication strategies. A qualitative study by Green et al. showed that digital opinion leaders play an important role in disseminating dengue prevention information, including in Indonesia [23]. However, most studies still build relationships between users from explicit interactions such as retweets and mentions, even though users who discuss similar topics do not necessarily interact with one another. Therefore, approaches based on multimodal embeddings that can capture content similarity remain underexplored. 2.3 Sentiment analysis of health content on social media Sentiment analysis of health content on social media can provide insight into how the public perceives a disease. In the case of dengue, Laguitan et al. [24] found that the quality and reliability of information circulating on YouTube vary widely, so not all sources have the same credibility and it is important to identify trustworthy sources. In Indonesia, Putri et al. [25] used IndoBERT to analyse public sentiment toward various public issues, whereas Mahakerty et al. [26] integrated Indonesian- language Twitter sentiment analysis into a deep- learning-based disease prediction model. These findings show that sentiment analysis can serve as a useful supplementary source of information for understanding the dynamics of disease spread in society. 2.4 Research gap Based on the literature review above, there are three research gaps centred on the suboptimal use of multimodal representations. First, research on multimodal sentiment analysis is still dominated by English-language data and rarely focuses on the Indonesian language, particularly in the health domain. Second, most multimodal methods rely on the audio modality, whereas the combination of text and visual thumbnails, which is precisely the primary signal on platforms such as YouTube, has not been widely studied. Third, the construction of co- audience networks to identify influential actors still depends on explicit interactions and has not exploited cross-modal content similarity, so the visual dimension that also determines content reach is overlooked. These gaps underscore the need for an Indonesian-language multimodal framework that explicitly combines the text and visual modalities to identify influential actors in the dissemination of dengue information on YouTube. Unlike previous research, the main novelty of this study lies in integrating IndoBERT text representations and ResNet-50 thumbnail visual features through Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF), which assigns adaptive per-dimension weights across modalities without relying on the audio modality. The resulting multimodal fused representation is then used to build a co-audience network based on content similarity rather than explicit interactions, and the contribution of each modality is verified through an ablation study so that the advantage of the multimodal approach can be demonstrated empirically against the unimodal text and visual baselines. 3. title: Examining Dengue-related Information Diffusion on Indonesian Twitter Through Sentiment-based Network Analysis, Spatial Mapping, and Temporal Dynamics
abstract: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited.This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025.Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions.Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98.Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values.Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles.These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis.

License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ Examining Dengue-related Information Diffusion on Indonesian Twitter Through Sentiment-based Network Analysis, Spatial Mapping, and Temporal Dynamics Ribka Devina Margaretha1 Wiwik Anggraeni1* 1Department of Information Systems, Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember, Surabaya, Indonesia * Corresponding author’s Email: wiwik@is.its.ac.id Abstract: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited. This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025. Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions. Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98. Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values. Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis. Keywords: Dengue fever, Sentiment-based network analysis, Spatial analysis, Temporal analysis, Social media. 1. Introduction Dengue fever remains one of the fastest- spreading vector-borne diseases and a major global public health challenge, endemic in more than 100 countries and threatening approximately 3.9 billion people, particularly in Southeast Asia and Latin America [1-3]. In Indonesia, dengue is highly endemic and continues to cause serious health problems, with more than 257,000 reported cases and over 1,400 deaths in 2024 [4]. The increasing spread of dengue, driven by climate change, urbanisation, and population growth, has also heightened public concern regarding outbreaks and prevention efforts [5]. The growing use of social media, particularly Twitter, has created new opportunities to observe public responses and information exchange related to disease outbreaks[6-8]. Through mentions, replies, and reposts, Twitter enables rapid information diffusion across communities, while certain accounts play disproportionately influential roles in shaping discussions [9]. Social Network Analysis (SNA) has therefore been widely applied to identify influential actors and examine information diffusion dynamics within online networks [10, 11]. Beyond interaction patterns, social media discussions also reflect public opinions and emotional responses toward ongoing health issues [12]. Sentiment analysis provides a complementary approach for capturing these perceptions, and incorporating sentiment information into network analysis can deepen understanding of how dengue- related discussions propagate and evolve on social media [13]. Dengue burden and public health responses are not uniformly distributed across Indonesia, with substantial disparities observed across provinces and Received: June 15, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 686 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ regions due to differences in population density, climate conditions, healthcare accessibility, and vector control capacity [14, 15]. Public perceptions and responses to health information also vary across communities due to cultural and social differences [16]. These regional variations highlight the importance of incorporating spatial information to better understand geographic differences in dengue- related discussions, public sentiment, and information dissemination patterns. Previous studies have applied SNA to identify influential users and examine information diffusion in online discussions, while sentiment analysis has been widely used to understand public perceptions toward health-related issues, and spatial analysis has been employed to reveal geographic variations in dengue transmission and public health responses. However, these approaches are typically investigated in isolation, limiting a comprehensive understanding of how interaction structures, public sentiment, and geographic context collectively shape online discussions. Studies integrating sentiment-weighted social networks with spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on Indonesian Twitter remain particularly limited, highlighting the need for a more integrated analytical framework. To address this gap, this study integrates sentiment analysis, SNA, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related Twitter discussions, constructing sentiment-weighted interaction networks and analysing them alongside geographic and temporal dimensions. The specific contributions of this study are: • Analysis of the spatial distribution of discussions and sentiments across Indonesian cities • Construction of sentiment-based interaction networks capturing both communication structure and public perception • Identification of national-level influential users using PageRank, degree centrality, and betweenness centrality • Identification of regional influential users across multiple Indonesian cities • Analysis of temporal discussion patterns and sentiment dynamics • Visualisation of interaction networks illustrating information diffusion structures. The remainder of this paper is structured as follows. Section 2 reviews related literature. Section 3 describes the data and methodology. Section 4 presents the results and discussion. Section 5 summarises the findings and outlines future directions. 2. Related works 2.1 Social network analysis for information diffusion SNA has been widely applied to investigate information diffusion and interaction patterns in online social networks, modelling users as nodes and interactions as edges to identify influential actors and community structures [17]. Various approaches have been proposed for influencer detection, including the NetDegree centrality measure and the Weighted Correlated Influence (WCI) model combining user activity and network topology [18, 19]. SNA has also been applied to explore community structures and communication dynamics in domain-specific discussions [20]. In health-related contexts, SNA has been used to identify key influencers, dominant topics, and communication structures shaping public awareness [10, 11, 21]. However, most existing health-related SNA studies focus on network topology and influencer identification without incorporating sentiment context or geographic variation. Bonifazi et al. identified influential users in COVID-19 vaccine Twitter discourse through a multilayer network approach, but did not construct sentiment-segmented networks or examine geographic distributions [21]. Durmaz and Hengirmen applied SNA to vaccine- related Twitter discourse in Turkey using in-degree and betweenness centrality, but did not integrate sentiment labels or examine spatial distributions [22]. Pratiwi et al. combined SNA and sentiment analysis for asthma-related Twitter discourse, but did not link findings to geographic distributions or construct sentiment-segmented networks [10]. The absence of sentiment integration and spatial context in these studies limits the depth of understanding achievable in health-related discourse analysis. 2.2 Sentiment analysis in social media discussions Sentiment analysis is widely applied to understand public opinions in social media, with recent studies demonstrating the effectiveness of advanced language models including IndoBERT for Indonesian-language content [23, 24]. Ishfaq et al. and Eliacik and Erdogan have incorporated sentiment into network-based analyses for influential user identification [25, 26]. However, applications combining sentiment and network characteristics in health-related discussions remain limited. Dengue-specific sentiment studies such as Abdul Ghani et al. demonstrate the value of sentiment for disease surveillance but do not Received: June 15, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 687 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ construct interaction networks or link findings to geographic distributions [27]. Indonesian-language classification studies such as Supriyadi and Makatita and Nabiilah et al. demonstrate strong model performance without connecting findings to network structures or spatial patterns [23, 24]. While Ishfaq et al. and Eliacik and Erdogan incorporate sentiment into network analyses, neither examined dengue- related discourse or linked findings to spatial distributions [25, 26]. No prior study has simultaneously applied sentiment-integrated SNA to dengue-related Indonesian Twitter data, leaving a gap in understanding how emotional responses and interaction structures collectively shape dengue information diffusion. 2.3 Spatial analysis in health-related studies Spatial analysis has gained increasing attention in public health and social media research for understanding geographic variations in behaviour and information dissemination. Lovera and Cardinale demonstrated that geolocation enriches the interpretation of social media discussions [34]. Similarly, Wu et al. highlighted the value of geospatial enrichment for understanding large-scale sentiment behaviour[35]. In health-related contexts, Lin et al. revealed linguistic and geographic disparities in COVID-19 public awareness through social media, while Zhang et al. applied geographical and temporal analysis to health-related tweets to identify spatiotemporal disease discussion patterns at regional level [36, 37]. However, these studies focus on geographic distribution patterns without modelling user interaction networks or identifying regional-level influential users. Lin et al., Zhang et al., Lovera and Cardinale, and Wu et al. all incorporate geolocation into social media analysis, but do not construct interaction networks, identify influential users, or examine how sentiment varies across network communities [z-37]. Studies applying spatial analysis to dengue-related social media discourse, such as Abdul Ghani et al., have similarly focused on geographic mapping without modelling user interaction dynamics or examining sentiment- segmented network structures [27]. The absence of interaction network modelling and sentiment integration limits understanding of how network dynamics and public sentiment collectively shape dengue information diffusion. 2.4 Research gap Despite the established contributions of SNA, sentiment analysis, and spatial analysis individually, existing health-related social media studies address these dimensions in isolation, as demonstrated across Sections 2.1 to 2.3, focusing on network topology without sentiment context [10, 21, 22], applying sentiment classification without network or spatial linkage[23, 27], or examining geographic patterns without modelling interaction dynamics [34-37]. While sentiment analysis and network approaches have each been applied to health-related social media discourse individually, their simultaneous integration with spatial analysis in the specific context of dengue-related Indonesian Twitter data remains unexplored. No prior study has proposed a unified framework simultaneously capturing the structural, emotional, and geographic dimensions of dengue-related information diffusion on Indonesian Twitter. This study addresses that gap by integrating sentiment analysis, SNA, and spatial analysis within a single framework, constructing sentiment- segmented interaction networks to examine how different emotional contexts shape network structure and influencer profiles, mapping discussion distributions and regional influencer patterns across Indonesian cities, and tracing temporal dynamics of both discussion volume and sentiment evolution over a five-year period. This integrated approach offers a more complete understanding of information dissemination patterns, influential users, and public perceptions across different locations and time periods than prior single-method studies have provided. 3. Materials and method 3.1 Dataset Dengue-related tweets were collected from Twitter (X) between January 2021 and December 2025 using the Scweet Python library with three keywords: "dbd" (dengue haemorrhagic fever acronym in Indonesian), "Aedes aegypti" (the dengue-carrying mosquito species), and "demam berdarah dengue" (dengue haemorrhagic fever). Data collection was conducted between 9-14 April 2026. The collected tweets span the period from January 2021 to December 2025, reflecting the full range of historical tweets retrievable through Scweet at the time of collection; Scweet retrieves historical tweets via browser automation rather than the official Twitter/X API, and collection completeness is therefore subject to the platform's search indexing and any rate-limiting constraints encountered during scraping. Collection was conducted as a series of discrete scraping sessions per keyword and sub-period, with no session returning a tweet count at or exceeding the configured retrieval limit (500-1,000 tweets, depending on keyword), indicating retrieval without truncation within each queried window. A completeness check was performed by examining the year-by-year distribution of collected tweets to confirm the absence of anomalous gaps or artificially uniform collection patterns; as detailed in Section 4.6.1, tweet volume varied organically across the five-year period, consistent with externally documented dengue activity patterns in Indonesia rather than indicating systematic data loss. Each tweet record contains textual content, publication date, user information, engagement statistics, and interaction attributes including mentions, replies, and reposts. The collected dataset serves as the primary source for all sentiment, network, spatial, and temporal analyses conducted in this study. 3.2 Method This study employs an integrated analytical framework consisting of data preprocessing, sentiment classification, network construction, community detection, spatial analysis, and temporal analysis. Data preprocessing The datasets collected from different periods were combined and filtered to retain only the attributes required for analysis, including tweet identifiers, usernames, tweet content, timestamps, language information, location attributes, and interaction metadata. User mentions and replies were extracted separately to support network construction. Duplicate tweets and records with missing values in essential attributes were removed, and tweet texts were cleaned through lowercasing, URL removal, mention and hashtag removal, number and punctuation removal, and whitespace normalisation. Tweets that became empty after cleaning were discarded, and only Indonesian-language tweets were retained. Examples of tweets before and after preprocessing are shown in Table 1. For spatial analysis, location information was obtained from tweet-level and user profile locations, with the latter used as a fallback when tweet-level location was unavailable. Location texts were normalised and matched against a reference dataset of Indonesian cities, with common aliases and abbreviations standardised to improve matching accuracy. This process successfully mapped 3,327 tweets (58.22%) to 168 Indonesian cities. 3.2.2. title_zh: 通过基于情感的网络分析、空间映射和时间动态检查印度尼西亚 Twitter 上与登革热相关的信息传播
source_body_en: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited.This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025.Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions.Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98.Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values.Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles.These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis.
abstract_zh: 登革热 仍然是印度尼西亚的一项重大公共卫生挑战,但整合情感分析、社交网络分析和空间分析来检查社交媒体上登革热相关信息传播的研究仍然有限。这项研究提出了一个综合框架,应用于 2021 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间从印度尼西亚 Twitter 收集的 5,715 条登革热相关推文。使用 IndoBERT 进行的情感分类显示,主要是中性话语 (65.23%),有意义的负面言论(20.31%) 和正 (14.45%) 比例。构建和建立了情感加权交互网络,揭示了高度碎片化的结构,模块化得分超过 0.98。医疗保健专业人员通过介数中心性成为最具影响力的参与者,基于 PageRank 的影响力以自循环 治疗 为条件,而卫生部拥有最高的入度值。空间分析,主要基于用户自我报告位置、表明爪哇-巴厘岛走廊沿线的地理集中度以及时间分析显示 1 月和 6 月反复出现的高峰与印度尼西亚的雨季和登革热 暴发 周期一致。这些发现证明了整合情绪、网络和空间维度对于全面公共卫生传播分析的价值。
